Latest Update: Elon Musk Interview At The DealBook Summit: Starlink Is Revolutionary And Saves Lives

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, stated at the DealBook Summit recently that “the number of lives that have been saved” by Starlink connectivity “may be hundreds.”.
  • Musk asked host Andrew Ross Sorkin, editor of DealBook, a daily business and policy report from The New York Times.
  • It was an ill-placed flippant comment, considering that Ukraine has suffered repeated disruptions to their access to Starshield — the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, stated at the DealBook Summit recently that “the number of lives that have been saved” by Starlink connectivity “may be hundreds.”.

Want to get the correct numbers? Musk asked host Andrew Ross Sorkin, editor of DealBook, a daily business and policy report from The New York Times. “It’s all over the internet. Just do a search.”.

It was an ill-placed flippant comment, considering that Ukraine has suffered repeated disruptions to their access to Starshield — the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink.

In an editorial following President Donald J. Trump’s meeting this week with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton reminds readers that, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian access to US early warning intelligence about incoming Russian missile strikes has been fractured, and Ukraine’s access to Starshield’s service remains limited.

Starshield helps Ukraine shoot down Russian attack drones. Limited access to Starshield means increased Ukrainian deaths as the country battles against Russian aggression — the opposite of Musk’s broad brush claim of lives saved by his technology.

Musk did address restrictions on the Ukrainian military’s access to the SpaceX satellite communications network during the Deal book Summit. He said that Starlink was never meant to be used for offensive strikes in war.

Historian and activist Rebecca Solnit refuses to dismiss Musk’s handling of Ukranian airspace as mere commerce. Elon Musk “has made much of his obscene pile of money off the US government with SpaceX and StarLink,” Solnit outlines. “They have given him power that should never belong to individuals – as demonstrated by his return to manipulating StarLink in ways that impair Ukrainian efforts in the war with Russia.”.

Representative Jim Himes (D-CT), the top-ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, has written to Elon Musk with a formal request “that senior SpaceX officials meet with me to explain the Starshield service disruptions in Ukraine in October 2026.”.

Industry observers note that himes notes that SpaceX, Musk’s company, is “a US Government purchased service established via a contract between the U.S. Government and SpaceX.” Himes wants to know “why those changes were made, and whether those changes were made unilaterally by SpaceX or were directed by a US Government official.” Since SpaceX has potentially modified a US Government contract, “combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight,” Himes argues that “every contract the US Government has with Space X” should be questioned.

It has been revealed that reducing the controversy to everyday terms, Musk insisted during the DealBook Summit that the Starlink design is “revolutionary,” in that it can be placed on a roof. “It solves the problem of reaching people who are in a building.” Sure, gaps in service continue, but Musk has a solution. “The missing piece of the puzzle” to making Starlink ubiquitous is an alternative to a metal roof, he suggested. The solution is “terrestrial… we can establish micro-ground stations… a network that are, maybe, bound together with Starlink terminals. Instead of big cell towers all over the place.”.

In a recent development, elon Musk is one of the richest people in the world, with significant political clout. He controls the direction and pace of one of the most crucial satellite technologies on which the US and the world depends, as former Secretary of Labor Robert Reich explains. Musk is one of the “authoritarians of the fresh economy,” Reich encapsulates, and Musk has “unparalleled power over every aspect of the lives of Americans and millions of others around the world.”.

Industry observers note that reich adds, “The Democrats should investigate why Elon Musk funneled a half-billion dollars into the 2026 midterms. Was it because he wants to keep his satellite monopoly? His defense contracts?”.

Musk has a lot on his mind these days. Sorkin reminded Musk that he had once remarked that his “mind was like a storm.”.

Musk responded that, right now, “I feel relatively at peace.”.

#145031. Common forever chemicals linked to nearly double the rate of aggressive breast cancer

Common forever chemicals linked to nearly double the rate of aggressive breast cancer

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that women with higher blood levels of two common "forever chemicals" may face an increased risk of developing a particularly aggressive form of breast cancer, according to new research from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), part of the U.S.
  • The study identified a connection between estrogen receptor-negative, or ER-negative, breast cancer and two widely encountered chemicals: perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS).
  • Both substances belong to a large family of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called PFAS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that women with higher blood levels of two common "forever chemicals" may face an increased risk of developing a particularly aggressive form of breast cancer, according to new research from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

The study identified a connection between estrogen receptor-negative, or ER-negative, breast cancer and two widely encountered chemicals: perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS). Women with greater concentrations of these substances in their blood were more likely to develop this type of cancer. However, researchers found no clear link between either chemical and breast cancer risk overall.

Both substances belong to a large family of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called PFAS. These chemicals have been used in numerous everyday consumer products and are often described as "forever chemicals" because they resist breaking down in the environment. They can also accumulate in the human body and remain there for years.

Industry observers note that "Women deserve clear answers about how chemicals in their environment may affect their health," remarked HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. "This NIH study links two forever chemicals to a higher risk of ER-negative breast cancer and demands further investigation. Under President Trump's leadership, we will pursue the evidence, confront environmental health risks, and give women the information they need to protect their health.".

Why This Aggressive Breast Cancer Is Concerning.

ER-negative breast cancer differs from more common forms of the disease because its tumor cells lack the receptors that allow estrogen to stimulate cancer growth. These cancers are often more aggressive and generally have poorer outcomes than tumors that respond to estrogen.

Despite their severity, researchers still have relatively little information about what makes someone more likely to develop ER-negative breast cancer. The latest findings suggest that exposure to certain persistent environmental chemicals could be one contributing factor.

"Our findings, which we confirmed using a meta-analysis of prior research, indicate that certain legacy PFAS, including PFOA and PFOS, are associated with a higher risk of ER-negative breast cancer, a more aggressive tumor type with few known risk factors," explained NIH Stadtman Investigator Alexandra White, Ph.D., who led the study.

The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology.

Higher Forever Chemical Levels Linked to Greater Cancer Risk.

To investigate the possible connection, NIH scientists and their collaborators examined blood samples that had been collected years before participants received a cancer diagnosis. The researchers measured concentrations of 17 different PFAS chemicals, allowing them to compare earlier exposure levels with subsequent breast cancer outcomes.

The results revealed substantial differences for two chemicals. Women in the highest PFOA exposure group had a 67% higher rate of ER-negative breast cancer than women in the lowest group. The association was even stronger for PFOS, with the highest exposure group showing a 93% higher rate, nearly twice that of the lowest group.

These percentages represent relative differences between groups rather than the absolute probability that an individual woman will develop breast cancer. The findings also establish an association, not proof that the chemicals directly cause the disease.

Recent findings suggest that the analysis used data from the Sister Study, a major research project conducted by NIH's National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS). Between 2003 and 2009, the study enrolled 50,884 women ages 35-74 from across the United States and Puerto Rico.

Sources indicate that all participants were free of breast cancer when they enrolled, although each had a full or half-sister who had already been diagnosed with the disease. For the PFAS investigation, researchers analyzed information from 1,609 women who subsequently developed breast cancer and a comparison group of 2,269 women.

Could Reducing PFAS Exposure Lower Cancer Risk?

Industry observers note that although PFAS can remain in the environment and the body for long periods, researchers emphasize that exposure is not necessarily unavoidable. The findings could eventually help identify fresh ways to reduce the risk of aggressive breast cancer.

"These findings matter for women's health broadly," stated first author, Che-Jung Chang, Ph.D., who previously worked as an NIH research fellow and is now a researcher at DLH, a scientific research organization. "Although PFAS are persistent in the environment and in our bodies, exposure to them is still potentially modifiable, meaning people can take steps to reduce their exposure, and these findings could open new avenues for prevention.".

The researchers are also interested in understanding how these chemicals might influence cancer development. Because the strongest associations appeared in tumors that lack estrogen receptors, the findings suggest that PFAS could act through biological processes unrelated to hormonal signaling.

Potential explanations include changes in gene activity or alterations in the immune system. However, the study did not directly investigate these mechanisms, so their involvement remains uncertain.

Newer Forever Chemicals Raise Unanswered Questions.

Although PFOA and PFOS have largely been phased out and replaced with other PFAS compounds, measurable amounts of both substances are still present in most people's bodies. Their persistence means that exposure to these older chemicals remains a potential public health concern.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers say additional investigations should focus on populations with greater PFAS exposure, as well as groups that experience higher rates of ER-negative breast cancer. Such research could help clarify the strength of the observed associations and identify whether certain populations face greater risks.

Scientists also need to determine whether the newer chemicals introduced as replacements for PFOA and PFOS carry similar health concerns.

"More research is needed, particularly evaluating the risk of breast cancer associated with newer replacement PFAS chemicals," White said.

The findings add to growing questions about the long-term health effects of forever chemicals and highlight the importance of understanding how environmental exposures may contribute to aggressive forms of breast cancer.

The research received support from NIEHS grants Z01ES044005; Z1AES103332; and R01ES032831.

Three Green Hydrogen Projects Slip Through The Trump Chopper

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1476 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when US President Donald Trump swept into office last year, he set his choppers upon the $8 billion Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program, snuffing out looks to establish a diversified, domestic hydrogen market with a focus on decarbonization.
  • Sources indicate that if you guessed the startup Plug Power is in the mix, run right out and buy yourself a cigar.
  • Plug Power soon pivoted into replacing gas-derived hydrogen fuel with so-named green hydrogen, pushed from water by an electrical current.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when US President Donald Trump swept into office last year, he set his choppers upon the $8 billion Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program, snuffing out looks to establish a diversified, domestic hydrogen market with a focus on decarbonization. Nevertheless, some stakeholders have continued to pursue the dream of producing green hydrogen from renewable resources — instead of squeezing it from natural gas. Now all that hard work is beginning to pay off, Trump or no Trump.

Sources indicate that if you guessed the startup Plug Power is in the mix, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. Plug Power began life back in 1997 with a focus on electric forklifts powered by zero emission hydrogen fuel cells. In addition to replacing fossil fuels, Plug Power aimed to replace battery-powered forklifts, with fuel cells being a better fit for the fast-paced environment of shipping and logistics.

Plug Power soon pivoted into replacing gas-derived hydrogen fuel with so-named green hydrogen, pushed from water by an electrical current. After a series of ups and downs the company hit the jackpot in January of 2025, when the US Department of Energy tapped it for a $1.66 loan guarantee in support of the Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs program, which was funded through the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. If all went according to proposal, Plug Power would have used the loan to finance up to six green hydrogen projects around the US, all affiliated with the Hydrogen Hubs program.

Industry observers note that so much for that. The Energy Department unveiled the loan award at the beginning of the month, when former President Joe Biden was still in office. However, by the end of the month Trump was officially installed in the White House. He soon pulled the plug on the Plug Power loan, so to speak, sending it down the drain alongside many other federally funded clean power projects.

It has been revealed that that was not the end of the story for Plug Power. After all, it’s a big world out there, and Plug Power continued to pitch its wares overseas. Last week the firm also relaunched itself back into the US market, bigly.

Industry observers note that on November 17, Plug Power revealed that its latest “GenEco™ Scale” green hydrogen electrolyzer system is up for grabs in the US market while concurrently announcing that its first customer is the Texas-based firm Aracdia eFuels. Arcadia will deploy 280 megawatts’ worth of GenEco Scale modules at its Project ARC campus in the Portland/Corpus Christi area in Texas. When fully up and running, Project ARC will deploy green hydrogen from the GenEco Scale system to produce about 23.2 million gallons of fossil-free aviation fuel per year.

While green hydrogen has its fans in the decarbonization field, the stubbornly high cost of electrolysis has raised a formidable obstacle against widespread commercial uptake. Plug Power is among the stakeholders pitching modular, integrated systems to help bring costs down into parity with conventional hydrogen sourced from natural gas or coal, and that’s where the GenEco system comes into play.

“Built around a standardized 20 MW block architecture, GenEco Scale combines Plug’s proven proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer technology with integrated balance-of-plant systems into a modular, pre-engineered solution for hydrogen production projects of approximately 100 MW and above,” Plug Power explained in a press statement last week. The tech giant also noted that the “outdoor-ready” system avoids much of the cost and time related to the buildings and other infrastructure required of traditional large scale electrolyzer systems.

Arcadia eFuels CEO Amy Hebert also chipped in her two cents in support of the modular system. “Reducing the engineering burden on our EPC [engineering, procurement, and construction] partners and minimizing the complexity of bringing these systems together were important considerations for Project ARC,” Herbert emphasized.

It has been revealed that savings on land is another part of the cost-cutting plan. Unlike conventional electrolyzer system layouts, the GenEco model deploys a vertical configuration. The vertical system requires less than one acre per 100 megawatts of electrolyzer capacity, according to Plug Power.

Another Plug Power project has bubbled up in California, which was on track to host a suite of projects under the Hydrogen Hubs program with a focus on hydrogen derived from biomass as well as water electrolysis. The funding evaporated under Trump, but the state is still getting its hands on green hydrogen.

On November 19, Plug Power declared that its containerized 5-megawatt GenEco electrolyzer is up and running at a green hydrogen plant in Vernon, California, under the umbrella of the Newly introduced Jersey-based firm Avina Clean Hydrogen.

Green hydrogen from this project will go to fulfill California’s aims for a zero-emission freight corridor, the initiative for which includes fuel cell electric trucks as well as battery-powered trucks. “Located approximately 10 miles from the Port of Long Beach, the facility is designed to serve fleets moving freight through the Los Angeles–Long Beach port complex. It combines on-site fueling with tube-trailer deliveries to customers across the Los Angeles region,” Plug Power explains.

The station, also accommodate buses, and it can refuel a heavy-duty vehicle to more than 95% capacity in less than 30 minutes, according to Plug Power. That stacks up well against charging times for battery-powered heavy duty vehicles. On its website, for example, Tesla asserts that its new Semi electric truck can recover 60% of its 500 mile range in up to 30 minutes at a Tesla Megacharger station.

For the record, Avina has not placed all of its cards on hydrogen fuel cell trucks. The tech giant’s roster of clean hydrogen projects also includes SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) and green ammonia, which is a key input for fertilizer among other chemical products.

Recent findings suggest that rounding out the trio of fresh projects is the Swedish firm PowerCell Group. The firm is better known for its work in the marine energy field, and now it is tapping into land-based markets as well. Last week PowerCell announced that its US branch is in motion to set up a green hydrogen system run by excess electricity from an existing solar array owned by a to-be-named client in the US. In effect, the hydrogen will serve as an energy storage medium. It will go to run a PowerCell PowerPod 3000 stationary fuel cell, which will kick into action at night to keep the clean kilowatts flowing after the sun goes down.

PowerCell describes the PowerPod 3000 as “a containerized power generation platform integrating our PS190 systems with power conversion equipment, cooling and DMC, PowerCell’s control and Energy Orchestration technology,” with an installed fuel cell capacity of 27 megawatts and 20 megawatts of rated power.

That’s a good question. Rather than let that excess solar electricity go to waste, the client could invest in a BESS (battery energy storage system) for daytime energy storage and night-time electricity. However, a typical BESS only lasts for a handful of hours. In contrast, PowerCell describes its fuel cell as a “long duration” storage system, which generally means eight hours or more.

PowerCell also points out that a fuel cell does something that a BESS cannot. Fuel cells generate electricity by combining hydrogen with oxygen in the presence of a catalyst. Water — H2O — is a byproduct. All else being equal, that opens up the potential for green hydrogen to serve as a water distribution medium, sucking up water in an electrolysis system at one location, then pushing it out in a fuel cell located elsewhere.

PowerCell is not making any specific promises for this particular project, though the organization does emphasize that “the ability to generate both electricity and recoverable water adds another dimension of value to hydrogen-based energy storage.”.

“The amount of water recovered, and its potential uses will depend on the final system configuration, operating conditions and water treatment requirements,” the organization adds.

In a recent development, and, that’s where things get interesting. The client is a to-be-named electric cooperative, which is of interest because electric cooperatives (more specifically, Rural Electric Cooperatives) account for a large portion of the US grid, and their roots in the rural poverty fighting programs of the Great Depression provide for a distinctive public benefit mission that can, in some cases, allow more wiggle room for innovative energy solutions that generate broad benefits for local communities.

It has been revealed that I’m reaching out to PowerCell for more details. If they can’t divulge the name of the client yet, perhaps they’ll be able to describe what they mean by long duration energy storage, so stay tuned for an enhancement.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, we asked our readers last week which road rage moments from their real lives most mirrored what they would see in "Grand Theft Auto 6." The responses in the comment section didn't disappoint with how bizarre, hilarious and terrifying these incidents were.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some people don't need to fire up "Grand Theft Auto 6" on a gaming console to experience the terror of a chaotic populace. The universe Rockstar Games crafted over two decades is over-the-top, but it has always been a satirical reflection of American society. This reflection also includes how quickly some of our fellow drivers are willing to resort to violence over the smallest grievance. However, our country's healthcare system hasn't discovered respawning despite how much money we've poured into it.

In a recent development, we asked our readers last week which road rage moments from their real lives most mirrored what they would see in "Grand Theft Auto 6." The responses in the comment section didn't disappoint with how bizarre, hilarious and terrifying these incidents were. Beyond the traditional roadside fistfights, we had a snowball toted like a handgun, altercations with actual firearms and BMW drivers reinforcing their terrible reputation. Without further ado, here are the incidents that wouldn't look out of place in Vice City:.

Back in HS, A friend of mine and I were driving around late night and while stopped at an intersection a guy in a Jeep took the corner really fast and almost sideswiped us. My friend gave him the middle finger out of the sunroof. Next thing we knew, we're in a high-speed chase involving the guy, who tried ramming us off the road multiple times. He caught us in a parking lot, blocked us from leaving and pointed a LARGE revolver at us. I grabbed my buddy's cell phone, held it up and screamed "I'm on the phone with the cops!" (even though I wasn't). That gave us enough time to drive over a curb, ripping his mufflers off, and drive up an embankment and high-tail it to the police station.

It has been revealed that moral of the story: Don't flip people off. Let it go and go on with your day.

A couple of years ago, I was walking through San Francisco's Embarcadero District on my way to Radwood NorCal (which was held on one of the piers that year). I overheard some yelling and turned my head to see a blue Jeep Cherokee XJ pulled over on the side of the road. The Jeep driver and a random homeless guy were in each other's face, yelling at each other. From what I made out, the driver accused the homeless guy of jaywalking right in front of him and spitting at his Jeep while the homeless guy argued that he was a pedestrian and that he had the right of way. Fortunately, it was just words being exchanged and no physical blows. The Jeep driver decided he had enough and took off with a loud squeal of tires.

It's so long ago that I don't remember what precipitated it, what happened, or how I behaved but here's what I do remember:.

Industry observers note that it was late afternoon. I was driving down 580 South through Berkeley, CA on my way to the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge. And here's how it ended: the other driver was on my left, his passenger-side window was open, and suddenly there was a VERY LOUD BANG from something hitting the side of my car. I hit the brakes so he'd shoot past me. He sped off, I kept my distance.

Later, I found a strange dent by the rear pillar (1997? Mazda Navajo LX (aka Ford Explorer Sport), like a thumb had pressed in the metal, but no hole in the metal or even the slightest break in the paint.

It has been revealed that I don't know, maybe he fired a .22 at me? A BB gun? Regardless, it was pretty frightening.

I was walking in downtown Chicago. A guy pulls to a stop at a red light at an intersection. He gets out of his car, nonchalantly walks up to a woman standing on the sidewalk waiting to cross the street, slaps her, then immediately walks calmly back to his car just as the light turns green, and drives away*. I assume they knew each other, because the woman did not react even a little, and continued just standing there with zero expression on her face.

*: He got instant karma, as there was a police cruiser 2 cars behind him, who then pulled him over on the next block.

About 15 years ago, my wife and I were sitting in her Chevy Cobalt in a parking spot in front of Hobby Lobby in Lincoln, NE during the holiday shopping season. It was snowing heavily (which will become crucial in a moment). We were on the phone with our cable company trying to figure out a billing error when another car pulls in next to us. The driver opens her door so hard it slams into our passenger door. I roll down the window and say something to the effect of, "Thanks for the door ding." Nothing demeaning. No name-calling. No F-you. Literally just sarcastically said what I said. Suddenly the husband comes flying around the car screaming at me, tries to open my door (which I swiftly locked), and when he realizes he can't get in goes to the front of the car and begins making a snowball out of the fresh snow. He literally holds his arm as if he is going to throw it at me while his wife joins in with the yelling. The cable company rep on our speakerphone is asking us if we need to hang up to call 911. We are in our car dying of laughter at this fool who is going to use a snowball as a weapon.

As they settle down and start walking into the store, we end our phone conversation and decide to exit our vehicle, as their loud yelling drew a small crowd, so we knew we would be safe. As I open my door, the husband and wife come flying back out of the store yelling at us for door-dinging THEIR car (I hadn't) and the husband slips in the snow and eats it. Serves him right.

Was first in line waiting to turn left on a red light that had an advance green. I heard sirens, so when the light changed to green I stayed still.

The 5 Series BMW behind me was blaring his horn and making a verbal commotion. Then he decided to swing around me on the right side to make the left-hand turn.

He was so busy looking at me sitting there that he almost didn't notice the ambulance right in front of him. (with lights and sirens). He slammed his brakes to a very sudden stop and the ambulance had to swerve around him.

According to recent reports, I saw him look in the rearview mirror at me. I smiled and waved.

This is more GTA San Andreas. I worked as a buyer in California for a large dealer that had blue uniform shirts (hint hint). My coworker was test-driving a customer car we were making an offer on, which was a bright blue Dodge Challenger with aftermarket matching blue rims.

In a recent development, he's sitting at a stoplight in his blue work shirt and bright blue car when a guy dressed completely in red, who was walking down the street, started yelling and running towards him. Luckily, the light turned green and my coworker gunned it before the guy got too close and things escalated further.

This was in the '90s. I was taking the Super Shuttle back to BWI from downtown DC and on the side of the road, a Mercedes and a BMW were pulled over and two dudes in suits were duking it out. Full-on fisticuffs in the breakdown lane, black eyes and bloody ties!

Sources indicate that stopped at a red light that had been red for about five seconds before I got to it. Dude in a black BMW 5 Series rolled up behind me and started blaring his horn. When that had no effect, he got out screaming with rage and started to approach my driver's door.

Sources indicate that at which time, seeing no cross-traffic, I accelerated through the red and called 911. He got back in his car, raced through the red after me. Being about six blocks from the police station, I told the operator not to bother sending the police: I'd bring him to them.

Sources indicate that he followed me right to the police station, tailgating me and blaring his horn the whole way as screaming out the window and giving me the middle finger. And boy was he in for a nasty surprise when we got there.

I love some cartoon violence. When I lived in Vancouver, a number of years ago, I'd just hopped off the bus downtown. A dude ran past me, reached out and snatched the purse off the shoulder of an older lady. He took off faster than I expected him to be able to run. If he'd just kept going, he'd have been home free. Instead, he looked over his shoulder to see if anyone was chasing him (three of us were)... and ran full speed into a glass bus shelter. Glass exploded everywhere, he hit the ground like wet cement and started bleeding from a decent head wound, and it was fantastic. Cartoon violence, instant karma, and a grateful lady who bought the three of us Starbucks for giving chase.

Teladoc Health is expanding its Comprehensive Weight Care program with a new option that allows employers to contribute to GLP-1 costs outside of traditional pharmacy benefit designs.

Through the upcoming offering, employers can give access to medications from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk—accompanied by support from licensed professionals, personalized lifestyle coaching, artificial intelligence-enabled food logging and more.

In a recent development, with each plan year, employers will set a fixed payment per employee per fill that applies consistently across covered medications, the firm said. Employees then pay the remaining balance for each fill. Teladoc manages eligibility, program oversight and consolidated invoicing.

Pharmacy claims are administered on a 100% pass-through basis, including eligibility verification and audit-ready claims documentation.

Moreover, employers can opt in to tie contributions to program engagement, using metrics like food logging and regular weigh-ins, executives say.

Industry observers note that the offering is available now, with initial contracted clients slated to launch programs for their employees beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

“Employers want to provide benefits that help their workforce achieve their health goals and need flexible strategies that work for their organizations,” stated Kelly Bliss, Teladoc Health U.S. Group Health president, in a statement. “We are helping employers meet the needs of their employees while providing greater predictability and transparency around healthcare spending. Importantly, we give people a trusted path to high-quality care and affordable access to FDA-approved, authentic medication for meaningful, sustained health outcomes.”.

Alongside the announcement, the firm also unveiled new research examining two years of weight-loss outcomes among nearly 23,000 members enrolled in its programs.

Results indicated “clinically meaningful weight loss” increased over time, with 47.7% of members achieving at least 5% weight loss by 24 months. And among those who lost weight during their first year, 53% continued losing additional weight during the second.

In a recent development, good morning! It's Monday, November 23, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most crucial stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition, Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia after resigning following affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and several employees, a handful of automakers are suing the great state of New Jersey to block an "extortionate" vehicle recall repair law, 1.6 million Hondas and Toyotas are impacted in the latest round of Takata airbag recalls and Amazon Autos is becoming a behemoth.

Nvidia's board of directors announced Monday morning that it would be unanimously reinstating Jensen Huang, who resigned in disgrace on November 12, as president and CEO following affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and at least two Nvidia employees. In a statement, the board noted the decision was made following a "series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA." Great.

Sources indicate that what's far more likely is President Trump stepping in, or, at least putting his thumb on the scale. The decision came just hours after the President wrote on social media, "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Firm, and also, for the U.S.A." I mean, the board pretty much said that was the case, with the caveat of "national security, saying Huang's reinstatement came after "input from senior levels of the United States government." It added that, based on the input, it was "confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." I'm sure the fact the stock dropped 46-ish% during this whole fiasco didn't impact the decision, either. As of publication, Nvidia's stock is up 33% today, and the S&P500 is up 5%. From NBC News:.

In his own statement, Huang said he was "honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.".

Huang has served effectively as the unofficial ambassador for the artificial intelligence boom, the companies backing it and the trillions of dollars being spent in the sector.

"I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support," Huang added.

Recent findings suggest that the reversal was a dramatic turn, after Nvidia's newly installed chairman Harvey Jones on Nov. 17 remarked, "Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO and Board member. The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Nvidia's inerim CEO Collette Kress also mentioned that the tech giant would not be reinstalling Huang in an interview the same day.

Huang's removal from Nvidia came after The Newly introduced York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. The Financial Times followed that report, saying that Huang had an affair with the woman.

Industry observers note that in a memo to Nvidia's workforce on Nov. 8, Huang remarked, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.".

The New York Times also reported Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior leader at Nvidia who reported directly to him.

After Huang's removal, the board of the organization initiated a search for a new leader, reportedly seeking out Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas. However, Haas earlier Monday announced that he was remaining at Arm, with a contract extension through 2033.

Nvidia also set up a new "national security and export control oversight" panel in light of the revelations about Huang.

Recent findings suggest that president Trump has already weighed in, saying on social media that the government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Attorney General Todd Blanche also confirmed that the government doesn't feel he broke any laws.

Still, Nvidia and Huang aren't out of the woods.

The return of Huang raises many questions for Nvidia, including the status of its dealings with overseas companies purchasing its high-powered chips, and Huang's relationships with his subordinates at the manufacturer.

Despite Trump's statement that the U.S. government believes that Huang poses no national security risk, the firm could still face legal exposure on other fronts. The Wall Street Journal and Reuters both reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is probing the company. The Journal said the probe was focused on the firm's accounting practices.

Industry observers note that in any case, Huang and his leather jackets are back. I'm sure everybody (the shareholders) is thrilled about that.

Ford, Honda, Stellantis and Volkswagen are suing the Great State of New Jersey (read: God's Country) in an effort to block a new state law that they say would increase the amount of money automakers would have to pay franchised dealers for warranty and recall repairs. Boohoo!!!!

In a complaint filed in Trenton, the capital of the world, the automakers mentioned the Fresh Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act gives dealers a "blank check" to set prices for warranty, recall and other repair services. They also contend that it prohibits them from avoiding "extortionate" results for recovering the costs. From the Detroit Free Press:.

New ⁠Jersey's law will shift more than $375 million a year to dealers from automakers, giving ​dealers a "windfall" by imposing no obligation to use the money to improve customer service or ​boost compensation for employees, the automakers said.

"In short, the act rewards dealers for charging their customers more," the automakers noted.

Fresh Jersey's law took effect on April 1, after ​former Governor Phil Murphy signed it in September 2025.

The automakers objected to letting dealers charge ‌a "labor multiplier" ⁠based on samples of repair orders, saying it lets dealers bill for substantially more labor time than they actually work.

They also challenged provisions requiring automakers to pay marked-up prices on parts that the dealers received at reduced cost or for free, and preventing automakers from ​providing less expensive ​parts even if supply, ⁠demand or other factors justified price cuts.

Ford, Honda, FCA — which includes Fiat and Chrysler — and Volkswagen remarked that since the law took ​effect, each has received dozens of bills requiring payment "for hours that ​no technician ⁠works, that surpass what comparable dealers charge for the same work, and that exceed what retail customers pay.".

They remarked the law violates the U.S. Constitution's Commerce Clause and Taking Clause, and it is preempted by federal laws governing recalls. They also contend it violates Newly introduced Jersey's Constitution. How dare they invoke New Jersey's Constitution? This thing of ours.

The Takata airbag disaster is a saga that will clearly never end, as evidenced by the fact that a further 1.6 million Hondas and Toyotas have just been recalled over airbag inflators that could rupture. Both automakers mentioned that no serious injuries or crashes have been tied to the recalled vehicles, and no ruptures have been reported, but out of an abundance of caution, they are replacing the inflators anyway. From Reuters:.

The recall includes 810,592 older Honda cars and ​SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States.

The Toyota recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 ‌IS250, ⁠2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner. The Honda recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles.

The Honda recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperature, humidity and large temperature fluctuations.

The vehicles ​in the current recalls have airbag inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material — unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously.

The National Highway ​Traffic Safety Administration mentioned analysis and inflator degradation simulation models conducted by independent testing groups allowed the automakers to act ahead of potential risks.

"Honda and Toyota saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are at the moment conducting proactive recalls of vehicles," NHTSA remarked ​late Friday, adding that other automakers continue to conduct inflator analysis and testing.

Honda said long-term ⁠monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions.

Toyota warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys and cause serious injuries.

The Honda recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, ⁠Florida, Georgia, ​Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Northern ​Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa.

Toyota did not specify in which US states the recall applies but said it expects the replacement inflators will be ​ready by early 2027.

Sources indicate that at least 28 people have been killed and over 400 have been injured by defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009 that send metal shrapnel inside the cars or trucks during inflation. It's an issue that prompted the largest automotive recall in U.S. history. All of those deaths involved airbag inflators without a dying agent, and at least 20 of those deaths were in Honda vehicles. Over the past decade, over two dozen automakers have recalled 100 million vehicles around the world, with about 67 million in the U.S. alone.

Amazon Autos streamlined its process to get dealers on its platform by more than 85 percent, replacing a one-size-fits-all signup page that left some dealers spending as much as a week registering for the digital sales platofrm. It helped overcome earlier problems that the platform has had since it launched at the end of 2024 that forced large dealership groups signing up on the same standarized page developed for standalone sotres and smaller groups. Now, there's a upcoming signup process for larger dealer groups, and it's causing the platform to baloon. From Automotive News:.

These brands also list used or certified preowned vehicles, along with 21 other vehicle makes.

Amazon Autos now has more dealers in the pipeline than they have live, [Amazon Autos director and global general manger Fan] Jin mentioned, and the organization continues to work through the backlog.

According to recent reports, dealerships are coming around partly because they now see Amazon as a reliable lead generator, rather than a competitive threat, said David Whiston, U.S. autos senior equity analyst at Morningstar Equity Research. It also helps, he said, that Amazon positions itself as assisting dealerships in selling vehicles rather than selling them directly to consumers.

Rohrman Automotive Group, with 20 dealerships in Indiana, Illinois and Wisconsin, sold 51 new and used vehicles through Amazon since it joined the partnership in April, said Jeremy Nowling, the group's sales and digital retailing director.

Sources indicate that amazon, for as significant a company as it is, also doens't seem too worried about how people use Autos. Some customers use the platform from start to finish, visiting the dealership just to puck up the vehicle. However, some start the process on Amazon and the visit the dealership to apply for financing or finish the process.

#145022. Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1034 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that vaccines may do more than protect people from the immediate effects of a viral infection.
  • Scientists at Pompeu Fabra University discovered that mice recovering from an acute viral infection experienced prolonged problems with their immune defenses.
  • Most people think of common viral infections, such as colds or stomach viruses, as temporary illnesses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that vaccines may do more than protect people from the immediate effects of a viral infection. Latest research suggests they could also help prevent lasting damage to the immune system that remains even after the virus has disappeared.

Scientists at Pompeu Fabra University discovered that mice recovering from an acute viral infection experienced prolonged problems with their immune defenses. Although the animals had successfully fought off the virus, their immune systems remained impaired, making it harder to respond to fresh threats. Remarkably, mice vaccinated before infection did not develop these problems, suggesting that vaccination may provide an additional layer of protection beyond preventing illness.

Most people think of common viral infections, such as colds or stomach viruses, as temporary illnesses. A virus enters the body, multiplies, causes symptoms, and is eventually brought under control by the immune system. Once symptoms disappear, recovery is generally considered complete. The immune response also creates protection against future encounters with the same virus.

But what if the immune system continues to experience harmful effects long after the infection appears to be over?

Viral Infections Can Leave Lasting Immune Damage.

Researchers from Pompeu Fabra University's Infection Biology Laboratory investigated this possibility in a study published in Cell Death & Disease.

In a recent development, using mice with acute viral infections, the team examined what happened to their immune systems after the animals had recovered. They found that eliminating the virus did not necessarily restore normal immune function. Instead, the infection left behind changes that persisted well beyond the initial illness.

In a recent development, according to Andreas Meyerhans, an ICREA research professor at UPF, who led the research, "there is a general perception that an acute viral infection is a relatively minor and transient event: once the virus is controlled and the symptoms have resolved, the body has fully recovered and is back to normal. But this view may underestimate consequences that are not immediately visible and can persist long after the infection itself has resolved.".

In a recent development, the researchers traced these lingering effects to significant changes in the spleen, an organ that plays an vital role in coordinating immune defenses. As the immune system fought to eliminate the virus, the spleen developed fibrosis, a condition involving the buildup of scar-like tissue. The arrangement and positioning of immune cells within the organ also became disrupted.

According to recent reports, these structural changes interfered with the interactions between immune cells that are necessary to activate T cells. These specialized cells are essential to adaptive immunity because they help recognize and destroy infected cells.

As a result, the mice remained less capable of launching effective immune responses when exposed to new challenges. Even though the original infection had been brought under control, their immune defenses continued to function poorly.

"The infection can be controlled, but that does not necessarily mean that the host has fully recovered," says Dr. Paula Cebollada Rica, first author of the study. "Our findings show that the immune-related consequences of an acute viral infection can persist beyond the period in which the virus is detectable, leaving the animals in an immunocompromised state.".

Vaccination Prevented Lasting Immune System Damage.

After identifying these long-term effects, the scientists investigated whether they could be avoided. They focused on vaccination, which prepares the immune system to recognize and fight a pathogen before an infection occurs.

The results revealed a striking difference between vaccinated and unvaccinated animals. Mice that received vaccination before infection did not develop the spleen damage or immune dysfunction seen in the other group.

Their spleens maintained their normal structure, and their T cells continued to function at levels comparable to those of mice that had never been infected.

It has been revealed that this finding suggests that vaccination can protect the immune system itself from some of the harmful consequences of fighting a viral infection. In the mouse model, vaccination not only protected against the disease caused by the virus but also preserved the animals' ability to respond to future immune challenges.

"Vaccinated animals did not experience T-cell dysfunction or splenic alterations after recovering from an acute viral infection. This means that vaccination not only prevented the disease resulting from the acute infection but also preserved the immune system's ability to cope with latest challenges," Cebollada Rica explains.

A Hidden Benefit of Vaccines With Public Health Implications.

According to recent reports, the findings broaden the potential benefits of vaccination by highlighting a form of protection that may not be immediately apparent. Beyond reducing the immediate effects of an infection, vaccines may also help prevent persistent changes that weaken immune defenses.

Although these results were obtained in mice and do not establish that the same effects occur in humans, they raise important questions about how viral infections influence long-term immune health and how vaccination might help protect it.

The research also comes at a time when vaccination policies and infectious disease prevention efforts are increasingly influenced by political decisions. The researchers emphasize the importance of scientific evidence in understanding the full consequences of infections, particularly when policy choices can undermine coordinated efforts to prevent infectious diseases.

Understanding the broader benefits of vaccination could therefore influence not only medical care but also how public health officials explain the value of vaccines to the public.

"The benefits of vaccination highlighted by this research are important not only for healthcare, but also for how we communicate the value of vaccination to the population at large," Meyerhans states. "It is important that people are aware of the broader protection that vaccination can provide and continue to trust in vaccines as one of the most effective tools to prevent diseases. Put simply, vaccines provide strong health benefits at a relatively low cost to society.".

Optum Rx rolls out new pharmacy tools aimed at transparency" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Earlier this year, Optum Rx teased the rollout of latest pharmacy tools designed to address medication cost and access.

Now, the company is offering a look at how those tools work.

It has been revealed that the pharmacy benefit manager stated Tuesday that the tools build on Optum's new and more transparent pharmacy model, which the company revealed in May and shifts to a fee-based structure. The model moves away from more traditional approaches linked to manufacturer pricing and prescription volume and offers clients a clearly defined fee structure.

The first platform, called Shop MyScript, allows members to compare prices for their medications as well as their options for pharmacies or delivery before the prescription is dispensed. The tool will notify members of potential cost savings shortly after a script is written.

In addition, Shop MyScript embeds in the prescribing workflow, Optum said, so that the member does not have to make comparisons after the fact. If they choose to keep the existing prescription, it will then be sent to the pharmacy.

Optum said that early adopters have averaged $28 in savings through the program.

"People should have clear information about their medication costs and options when they can actually use it, not after a decision has already been made," remarked Katte Carey, president of Optum Rx, in the announcement. "These tools give people more information earlier in their journey, so they can make choices that work for them and get the support they need along the way.".

In addition, the pharmacy benefit manager declared Optum Assistant, a conversational AI guide that helps members complete routine tasks and track down key information. The tool can triage concerns on a range of topics, from questions about medication and benefits to pharmacy experience challenges.

Industry observers note that if the AI guide can't address the individual's needs, they can choose to be connected to live support to find a solution. Optum noted about 80% of conversations using the tool led to a resolution without needing a live advocate.

The final newly introduced launch aims to support cash-pay options, according to the announcement.

Recent findings suggest that optum Price Wise will offer members a complete cost breakdown, including the price of a drug and any fees. That total, all-in price allows members to fully understand what their options may be and make the choice that works best for them at the pharmacy counter.

The PBM remarked newly introduced tools like these build on Optum's new and more transparent pharmacy model, which the tech giant announced in May and shifts to a fee-based structure. The model moves away from more traditional approaches linked to manufacturer pricing and prescription volume and offers clients a clearly defined fee structure.

According to recent reports, army notes it plans to detonate degraded lead in Iowa town no later than Nov. 24, despite court stay.

In a recent development, des Moines, IOWA — The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club, and Earthjustice will continue to advocate for accountability from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army in the planned detonation of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa. Early Sunday morning, the groups filed declarations with the court that call out the Army’s inadequate public notice and information, and question the Army’s and EPA’s claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a statement with the court late on Saturday, Nov. 21, indicating that the Army intends to invoke emergency provisions of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) to detonate 9,773.5 pounds of lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunitions Plant, without a permit from the EPA. According to the DOJ’s court filings, the Army intends to do so no later than Nov. 24. On Nov. 20, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals granted Earthjustice’s request to put on hold a permit allowing the Army to detonate.

Industry observers note that “People across numerous impacted communities speaking up and demanding accountability is the only reason there was an opportunity to pause and think about better ways to approach the lead azide problem,” noted Earthjustice Attorney Thien Chau. “Yet despite claiming public safety is its top priority and public communication is essential to trust, the Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm.”.

Sources indicate that this emergency is of the Army’s own making. The Army has not publicly provided details about why the lead azide was not disposed of before it became so dangerous. The Army’s own storage and inspection practices allowed a primary explosive to sit until it reportedly degraded to the point that any alternative disposal method is now deemed too dangerous. The lack of transparency raises real questions about the scope and extent of potential impacts.

Sources indicate that “The fresh information from the DOJ indicates that the problem is significantly worse than the Army originally shared. It appears that detonation may be, at this point, the only feasible option due to how long this problem was allowed to persist. The public deserves to know immediately which communities will be impacted and how residents can most effectively protect themselves and mitigate impacts on their health and homes,” mentioned Michael Schmidt, General Counsel for the Iowa Environmental Council.

The Army knew about this stockpile of dangerous munitions waste for years, and it knew since at least March that the material was becoming unstable. Yet, just one week ago, most Iowans — including those directly in the path of a toxic lead plume, the Iowa governor, and key state agencies and officials — were unaware the Army intended to detonate nearly five tons of lead azide.

The environmental groups argue the EPA and Army permitting documents have not demonstrated, nor provided appropriate documentation that all other safer alternatives to mitigate the material were thoroughly explored.

Industry observers note that “The Army has clearly mishandled this situation, and Iowans and residents in our neighboring states deserve a full review of all of the missteps that led us to this point. However, if detonation is now the only option, it is imperative that everyone impacted has access to the full range of testing, mitigation, and remediation resources,” stated Wally Taylor, Attorney and Legal Chair for the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter.

Sources indicate that as of 11 a.m. CST on Sunday, Nov. 22, the Army has failed to provide the public with updated weather modeling and mapping showing the path of the lead dust plume, which means people impacted have little time to take precautions to protect their families and homes. The wind patterns have shifted significantly, which means that potential community exposures have likely changed without visible effort by the Army to provide updated information to the public.

Medicare Shared Savings Program saved $2.5B last year: CMS" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

The Medicare Shared Savings Program has reached the highest savings number in its history, according to new federal data.

Recent findings suggest that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services said Tuesday that the program generated more than $2.5 billion in net savings for Medicare in 2025, making for the ninth year in a row that it led to cost savings. The agency added that every accountable care organization met or exceeded quality reporting requirements.

ACOs participating in MSSP earned $4.9 billion in shared savings payments during 2025, CMS stated, with 80% of organizations earning performance payments.

As of 2026, 511 ACOs representing more than 700,000 providers are participating in the Medicare Shared Savings Program, which represents 12.6 million people enrolled in traditional Medicare, another record.

"Patients want doctors who work together, care that puts their needs first, and fewer unnecessary hurdles—that is what accountable care is designed to deliver," said CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, M.D., in the announcement. "These record savings show the power of rewarding providers for quality and coordination. We want more people with Medicare, and more of the providers who care for them, to benefit from this approach.".

CMS said that it wants to make it easier for providers to participate in MSSP if they choose, especially given the program's results to date. It included changes in the latest Physician Fee Schedule to encourage participation, including increased opportunity for certain ACOs to earn shared savings and latest financial incentives to draw in first-time participants.

According to recent reports, in addition, CMS mentioned that would create more predictable spending targets that make planning and participation straightforward. The agency is also aiming to streamline patient notices and simplify required technology.

Recent findings suggest that “We are excited to see continued progress on both savings and enrollment for Medicare beneficiaries. Beneficiaries are best served when a provider is watching out for them and coordinating their care,” said Center for Medicare Director John Brooks in the announcement.

Emily Brower, CEO of the National Association of ACOs, said in a statement that the 2025 results "build on years of progress and underscore what the accountable care community can accomplish through collaboration, innovation and the widespread adoption of proven best practices.".

It has been revealed that "NAACOS looks forward to partnering with CMS to build on this momentum," said Brower. "Policies that unleash innovation, reduce burden, and create sustainability through fair and predictable budgets will allow ACOs to deliver even greater value for patients and the Medicare program.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 climate talks break down reveals that fossil fuel interests remain a major obstacle to climate action.

Recent findings suggest that the lack of a final text at the end of COP31 shows how far the fossil fuel industry is willing to go to keep its polluting businesses operating, says T&E. While the final text of COP28, in 2023, called for ‘transitioning away from fossil fuels in the energy system’, fossil-producing countries have blocked similar language in subsequent COPs despite the growing economic and social costs of climate change.

Sources indicate that antony Froggatt, senior director at T&E, mentioned: “In a year marked by record oil prices and extreme temperatures, fossil fuel companies moved to block any agreement calling for a phase-out of oil, gas, and coal. They did so to protect their commercial interests even as solar and wind already power the majority of the grid in countries worldwide, and electric vehicles make up nearly half of upcoming car sales in the world’s largest auto market.”.

It has been revealed that this is not the end of the international processes, and the Paris Agreement remains in place. The next COP will take place in Ethiopia, and the phase-out of fossil fuels will once again be discussed. In the meantime, the Santa Marta process, which grew out of COP30’s failure to agree on a fossil fuel roadmap, will once again meet, and it is expected that countries representing one-third of the world’s economy will debate and develop practical ways to move away from coal, oil and gas.

Recent findings suggest that analysis by T&E at the beginning of the week shows that EVs displace five times more oil globally than they did five years ago. Battery-electric vehicles already displace 1.2 million barrels of oil a day and avoid more than 200 Mt of CO2-equivalent a year.

“Petrostates’ chokehold on COP31 underscores the need for the progressive majority to continue pushing for international co-operation and global targets on electrification that can accelerate decarbonisation while improving energy security, air quality and economic prosperity,” added Antony Froggatt.

“The same oil shock that delivered record profits for the oil industry has pushed up costs for the world’s most vulnerable countries, most of which import their fuel. Governments should make the polluter pay. Excess profits should be heavily taxed, and the revenue used to fund electrification and climate resilience where it is needed most,” he concludes.

Five Fuel-Sipping Tips That No One Else Has The Guts To Suggest

💡 Key Takeaways
  • America's affordability crisis doesn't seem to be going away any time soon, with everyone's budgets getting battered left and right by inflation, record-high housing costs, war-driven fuel price hikes, and sky-high automobile operating costs.
  • In a recent development, obviously, the most fuel-efficient thing to do in a cash crunch is to drive less, take public transit, or get there without burning fuel on foot or by bicycle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

America's affordability crisis doesn't seem to be going away any time soon, with everyone's budgets getting battered left and right by inflation, record-high housing costs, war-driven fuel price hikes, and sky-high automobile operating costs. It's starting to feel a lot like the 2008 financial crisis out here in the streets again. I distinctly remember everyone suddenly caring about their fuel economy back then, scrambling for more fuel efficient cars. With new car prices higher than ever, that might not even be an option for you. So let's look into a few measures you can implement on any car to make it more efficient.

In a recent development, obviously, the most fuel-efficient thing to do in a cash crunch is to drive less, take public transit, or get there without burning fuel on foot or by bicycle. If those aren't viable options for you, even the least efficient transportation machine can benefit from these five suggestions. And if you're getting 12 miles to the gallon right now, bumping that up to 13 or 15 could make a pretty significant difference to your weekly budget.

For example, at the current national average fuel price of $3.81 per gallon, a vehicle that gets 12 mpg combined and travels 15,000 miles a year (the EPA's annual estimate), would spend $4,762.50 a year on fuel, while bumping that to 15 MPG would mean spending $3,810 per year — that's a massive annual savings.

Here are five great ideas that you should definitely implement for your car to achieve better fuel economy. Some are more, um, involved than others, so before you dive into a project, make sure you have the necessary tools, skills, materials, time, space, and mental fortitude. You can absolutely do some of these projects yourself, but others might be best reserved for a professional, at which point you'll have to weigh the cost of modification against savings.

In a recent development, here in the United States, the midterm elections finished up, and if you live in a swing state, as I do, you were probably bombarded with political ads, and seemingly every yard had signage for an election campaign or a ballot measure. Most of those signs are made from a corrugated plastic material called coroplast, which is significant for its low weight and high strength. That combination makes them great for constructing your own DIY aerodynamic modifications. Getting the materials for free is just an added benefit.

It has been revealed that if you've been under a car before, you know that it's a lot less smooth than the shiny side you look at every day. There are exhaust pipes, suspension, driveshafts, and jacking points. If you manage to get a couple of the really significant (and really obnoxious) yard signs, you could build a nice aerodynamically efficient flat floor tray for your car, improving the efficiency of airflow between the bottom of your car and the road. Tie it in to your rear bumper, and you'll help prevent a lot of turbulence.

In a recent development, it should go without saying that your car's exhaust gets pretty hot under normal operation, hot enough to melt coroplast. You should build your flat floor in a way that the inexpensive plastic material is mounted far enough away from the exhaust to prevent melting, perhaps even with a heat shield material to protect the edges. It's also possible that political signs in your area aren't made of coroplast, so be careful when you're using unconfirmed plastic to block off your engine bay from airflow or releasing heat. To get a proper flat floor around the exhaust pipes, you can use sheet aluminum in hot spots to keep the airflow clean and prevent melting.

After your flat floor, if you have some more coroplast laying around, you can build for yourself a grille block off. Because your car was built from the factory to operate in any temperature range, it has to have a larger grille opening and radiator than you need for light duty operation, particularly in the colder months.

Industry observers note that not only does selectively blocking airflow through the grille help improve the aerodynamic efficiency of your car at highway speeds, it will also help your car's engine warm up faster than it would with the radiator exposed to cold air. A cold engine consumes far more fuel than a warm one, so a faster warm-up time and maintaining heat within your engine compartment during trips with multiple stops is more beneficial to fuel economy than you might think.

In a recent development, you may have seen this sort of modification on diesel trucks and big rigs, especially in extremely cold temperatures. This is an easy one to get wrong, particularly if you forget you have a grille blockoff and leave it in through summer, so you'll have to pay attention to your car's gauges to avoid overheating. If you use them properly, you'll gain some winter MPGs. Again, it's key you know what you're doing with this project, as it is extremely easy to implement, but just as easy for it all to go awry.

According to recent reports, many automakers have employed expensive motorized grille shutters in an effort to improve efficiency. If you're really smart with electronics, you might even be able to craft your own motorized grille shutters with thermostatic controls that can potentially help improve your fuel economy in all seasons.

Chopping a section out of the middle of a car's height to lower the roof is a tried-and-true hot-rodding mod. While primarily used for looking cool, chopping the roof a few inches helps in many aspects of performance driving. Not only does it lower the car's center of gravity, but it reduces the frontal area of the vehicle, making it slip through the wind better. Improved aerodynamics are good for going fast, as your top speed improves, but it's also good for efficiency, as the car's overall aerodynamic drag goes down.

According to recent reports, in the video above, the Motor Mythbusters made a dramatic chop to an old Dodge Tradesman van. Perhaps taking things to extremes is the best way to show their efficacy. It doesn't take a scientist to figure out that a Tradesman isn't very aerodynamic, isn't very fast, and isn't very efficient. By increasing its quarter-mile trap speed by several miles per hour, the team proved a chopped top was more aerodynamic.

Sources indicate that if you can cut through the air better, you need less power to maintain a normal highway speed, reducing your fuel consumption. If you want to get really wild with it, you can reduce your frontal area even more by making your car a single-seater and cut the greenhouse of the car in half down the middle, like this Geo Metro owner did.

Obviously, there are some practical downsides to chopping your roof. For one thing, it's hard to recommend cutting the structural pillars of your car, just for the effect it might have on the car's rollover safety. Modify at your own risk.

It has been revealed that bulky exterior mirrors are one of the areas where automakers have sought to reduce aerodynamic drag for decades. In order to comply with government safety regulations, the mirrors need to show what's happening behind you, and for a number of different seating positions, requiring them to be quite large and adjustable. As the owner of the car, you can theoretically modify your car with smaller aftermarket mirrors, reducing the frontal area of your car further than the factory could in the development phase. But what if you could get rid of your mirrors altogether?

Audi, a few years ago, introduced its "virtual mirror" technology on the old e-Tron SUV. It wasn't permitted for use in the U.S. market, but it did go on sale elsewhere. By swapping the giant mirrors for a compact camera on an arm, Audi claimed the reduction in drag (dropping the e-Tron's cD from 0.28 to 0.27) was good enough for a couple of percentage points in overall vehicle efficiency. The camera relayed exterior images to a small real-time video screen in each door. The system, while expensive, allowed Audi to bump the car's range numbers by four miles.

According to recent reports, because aftermarket modifications aren't mandated to follow the same strict regulations as OEM equipment, you could theoretically suction cup some GoPros on the outside of your car and have them relay the video via Bluetooth to your phone. Or, you know, you could do something a bit nicer and with less latency. Who wants a delay when you need to know if it's safe to merge? Maybe you could 3D print a little housing for a small lens and run some wire through the mirror hole to feed a dash-mounted video monitor? I've been looking into something like this for a future project of my own.

In a recent development, weight is the enemy of efficiency, and modern cars have gotten quite heavy. The U.S. Department of Energy says carrying an extra 100 pounds of weight in your car can reduce your fuel economy by one percent. One side of that is to reduce as much of the cargo you're hauling around without needing to, so if you've been meaning to donate stuff to Goodwill and it's been in your trunk for a month, you've been taking a fuel economy hit as a result. On the other side, every pound of unnecessary weight you can remove from your car makes your car more efficient.

Recent findings suggest that making your car lighter helps in every aspect of driving. A lighter car accelerates easier, meaning it'll require less fuel to gain speed at a given rate. It also means you can carry more speed through corners, reducing the need to brake and accelerate again. A lighter car is also easier on your consumable components, easing the efforts on brake pads and rotors, tires, and suspension components. An engine that isn't laboring quite as much will also wear less rapidly and theoretically last longer.

It has been revealed that so what can you do to reduce weight? I guess it depends on how much you can live without. A fully stripped interior with little more than a driver seat is going to be several hundred pounds lighter than one that's complete. If you can live without things like a center console, a stereo, a dashboard, and more, you could save a lot on fuel. If you want to be a little more pragmatic about it, there are still things you could do. You drive a minivan with a removable row of seats? You could save some fuel by removing those seats when you don't need them.

Sources indicate that did you always want to be a car designer when you grew up? Thanks to advances in 3D scanning technology, computer-aided design, computational fluid dynamics, additive construction, and instant-quote small-batch manufacturing, it's possible to design and build your own car's bodywork to your own exacting standards. Of course, you'll have to learn how to manipulate the software in order to make that happen, but it's definitely possible. Say you wanted to add an aerodynamic boat-tail or wheel skirts to your car, like the Volkswagen Mission Efficiency concept shown above. It's all within your reach!

A boattail shaped rear end is the most aerodynamically efficient way for a car to cut through the air. Not only does this allow air to continue to stay attached to the car, but it gives a smooth transition to clear air after the car goes through. An abrupt trunk with a blunt cutoff will create lots of turbulence behind it, which acts like a vacuum sucking the car's forward progress. By shrinking the low pressure area at the back of the car, there's much less pressure drag. Adding a five-foot boattail extension behind a semi-truck, for example, has been shown to increase fuel efficiency by almost twelve percent!

Sources indicate that similarly, wheel skirts help remove turbulent air from the car's trajectory through the air. Ecomodder logs show a few DIY wheel skirt projects with improvements from one to two miles per gallon, depending on application. Rear wheel skirts are much easier to install than fronts, as the front wheels need to exit the cover of the fender when turning, while the rear wheels are always covered. By filling in the gap between the fender and wheel, reducing drag, the car's engine doesn't have to work as hard to accelerate or maintain speed, improving economy.
