General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realtybiznews ↗ Open Full Page

Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

📅 07 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (722 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtybiznews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients.
  • The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience.
  • The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

Sources indicate that when writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

Industry observers note that in the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Industry observers note that social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

Sources indicate that to encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

In a recent development, an effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt users to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

According to recent reports, writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

#144928. Latest Update: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1495 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1495 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits.
  • Recent findings suggest that researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease.
  • Sources indicate that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits. Although heavy drinking was linked to worse health outcomes regardless of the beverage, the picture was more complicated among people who consumed smaller amounts of alcohol.

Recent findings suggest that researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease. In contrast, similar amounts of beer, cider, and spirits were linked to a higher risk. The findings, presented at the American College of Cardiology's Annual Scientific Session (ACC.26), suggest that both the type and quantity of alcohol may influence its relationship with long-term health.

Sources indicate that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health. Importantly, the new findings do not establish that wine itself protects against disease.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," stated Zhangling Chen, MD, PhD, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author.

How a Study of 340,000 Adults Measured Alcohol Risk.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate the relationship between drinking habits and longevity, scientists examined data from 340,924 adults enrolled in the UK Biobank between 2006 and 2022. The UK Biobank is a large research resource that collects health and lifestyle information to help scientists investigate factors associated with disease and mortality.

In a recent development, participants reported their alcohol consumption through dietary questionnaires when they joined the study. Researchers then classified them into four groups based on how much pure alcohol they typically consumed each day or week, rather than simply counting drinks.

This distinction matters because beer, wine, and spirits contain different concentrations of alcohol. For comparison, a 12-ounce can of beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of spirits each provide approximately 14 grams of pure alcohol.

People consuming fewer than 20 g (about 1.5 standard drinks) per week were placed in the never or occasional drinking group. Low consumption was defined as 20 g per week up to 20 g per day for men, and 20 g per week up to 10 g per day for women.

Moderate drinking was defined as 20 g to 40 g (about 1.5 to three standard drinks) daily for men and 10 g to 20 g daily for women. High consumption meant more than 40 g (about three drinks) per day for men or more than 20 g (about 1.5 drinks) per day for women.

Researchers followed participants' health outcomes for an average of more than 13 years, allowing them to examine how drinking patterns were associated with deaths from different causes.

Wine, Beer, and Spirits Show Different Heart Health Risks.

It has been revealed that the clearest finding concerned heavy alcohol consumption. Compared with people who never drank or consumed alcohol only occasionally, heavy drinkers had a 24% higher risk of dying from any cause. Their risk of dying from cancer was 36% higher, while their risk of dying from heart disease was 14% higher.

These increased risks were associated with heavy drinking regardless of whether participants preferred wine, beer, cider, or spirits.

However, the results became more surprising when researchers examined low and moderate alcohol consumption. At these levels, the type of beverage was associated with substantially different outcomes.

People who consumed wine in low to moderate amounts had a significantly lower risk of death, while those who consumed comparable amounts of beer, cider, or spirits had a significantly higher risk.

It has been revealed that the contrast was especially striking for cardiovascular disease, a broad category of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease than people who never or only occasionally drank alcohol.

By comparison, even low consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was associated with a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

According to recent reports, these percentages describe relative differences in risk between groups, not the absolute probability that an individual will die from cardiovascular disease. Because the research was observational, the findings also cannot demonstrate that choosing one alcoholic beverage over another directly changes a person's risk.

"Our findings help clarify previously mixed evidence on low to moderate alcohol consumption," Chen remarked. "These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed, but also on the type of beverage. Even low to moderate intake of spirits, beer, or cider is linked to higher mortality, while low to moderate intake of wine may carry lower risk.".

Why Might Wine Be Linked to Lower Heart Risks?

Researchers identified several possible explanations for the differences, including the chemical composition of wine and the habits of people who drink it.

Red wine contains polyphenols, naturally occurring compounds found in plants that can have antioxidant properties. Antioxidants help counter certain chemical reactions involving unstable molecules that can damage cells. Some polyphenols have been investigated for potential benefits to blood vessels and cardiovascular function.

These compounds could contribute to the associations observed in wine drinkers, although the study did not establish that they were responsible for the lower mortality risk.

Another possible explanation involves how and when people drink.

Wine is more commonly consumed alongside meals, and wine drinkers often report healthier diets and lifestyle habits. Drinking wine may therefore be associated with other behaviors that support cardiovascular health.

Beer, cider, and spirits, on the other hand, are more frequently consumed outside of meals. In this study, people who favored these beverages also tended to have poorer overall diet quality and other lifestyle factors associated with increased health risks.

Such differences make it difficult to separate the effects of the alcohol itself from the characteristics and habits of the people consuming it.

"Taken together, these factors suggest that the type of alcohol, how it is consumed, and the associated lifestyle behaviors all contribute to the observed differences in mortality risk," Chen noted.

What the Findings Mean for Alcohol and Health.

Industry observers note that to make their comparisons more reliable, the researchers statistically adjusted their analyses for numerous factors that might influence mortality. These included age and other demographic characteristics, socioeconomic circumstances, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic health.

According to recent reports, cardiometabolic factors include conditions and measurements related to heart and metabolic health, such as blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, and cholesterol levels. The analyses also accounted for family histories of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

Even with these adjustments, the researchers emphasized several vital limitations.

Because the study was observational, it could identify associations between alcohol consumption and mortality but could not prove that particular beverages caused better or worse outcomes. Other differences between participants may have influenced the findings despite the statistical adjustments.

Alcohol intake was also measured through questionnaires completed when participants first entered the study. That information depended on participants accurately reporting their own drinking habits, and it did not capture changes in consumption during the years that followed.

Another consideration is that UK Biobank participants tend to be healthier than the general population. This could limit how well the findings apply to other groups of people.

The researchers suggested that high-quality randomized trials could provide stronger evidence about the health effects of different drinking patterns. Such studies would help clarify whether the observed differences reflect the beverages themselves or other factors associated with their consumption.

Nevertheless, the enormous study population and more than 13 years of average follow-up provide considerable statistical strength. By examining specific types of alcohol, different levels of consumption, and multiple causes of death, the research offers a more detailed picture of alcohol's potential health risks than many earlier investigations.

The findings highlight an crucial distinction: while heavy drinking is consistently associated with harmful health outcomes, the relationships observed at lower consumption levels may depend on beverage choice, drinking habits, and broader lifestyle patterns.

In a recent development, for now, the apparent advantage among wine drinkers should not be interpreted as a reason to start drinking wine for heart health. The evidence points to a complex relationship between alcohol and mortality, rather than proving that any alcoholic drink offers protection.

Ziyue Li presented the study, "Alcohol Use at Mid-Life and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality," at ACC.26.

The Rise of the House Manager: Why Busy Families Are Outsourcing Everyday Tasks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.
  • For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.
  • For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.

For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.

For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.

"A house manager takes on the parts of the household a family chooses to hand off—that means both the everyday work and the planning behind it, from start to finish," states Kelly Hubbell, founder and CEO of Sage Haus, a thriving house manager placement manufacturer. "Think meals, laundry, errands, calendars, pet care, and home projects. A house manager doesn't just complete tasks ... they anticipate what's needed and handle it without being asked.".

In other words, a house manager is an added support system that helps keep a household functioning efficiently.

The simplest definition of a house manger is someone who helps facilitate everyday life behind the scenes.

"A housekeeper cleans, a nanny cares for the kids, a house manager owns whole areas of the household, from planning to follow-through," says Hubbell.

It has been revealed that there can be overlap. A house manager might tidy, do laundry, or prepare meals, depending on what the family hands off. The difference is ownership.

"Take laundry: A housekeeper might wash what's in the basket, whereas a house manager who owns laundry knows the soccer uniform has to be clean by Saturday, without a reminder," explains Hubbell. "The work that's different is the thinking behind the household.".

The best house managers have sharp judgment and the ability to blueprint ahead, juggle several schedules and tasks at once, manage vendors, and make good decisions within the scope a family has agreed to, according to Hubbell.

According to recent reports, they're proactive and notice what needs attention before anyone asks. And because they're in someone's home, trust, reliability, and discretion are essential.

In a recent development, "People come to it from lots of backgrounds: nannies whose kids aged out of needing a nanny, teachers, hospitality and operations managers, military spouses who have set up a household in four cities, and moms coming back into the workforce after years of running their own homes—frankly, the hardest training there is," says Hubbell, whose network now includes over 7,000 house managers in the U.S. and Canada, though Sage Haus accepts only about 5% of applicants to ensure quality.

"As AI changes the jobs available, this work depends on what technology can't supply: human judgment, trust, and care," she explains.

Basically, house managers are gaining traction because people are burning out, especially women.

"Most families hit a point where their life, career, or ambitions can't grow any further without more support—I call that the support ceiling," states Hubbell. "They don't need to scale back their dreams. They need to scale up their support.".

Many families already have some help, like a cleaner every other week, a nanny/sitter, or groceries on autopilot. But someone still has to hold it all together—the noticing, planning, and following up.

"That's the mental load, and research indicates it usually stays with mom, even as her career and earnings grow," says Hubbell.

According to a 2024 study from the University of Bath and the University of Melbourne, mothers in the U.S. carry 71% of mental-load tasks, and while women’s employment and earnings reduce their physical household labor, it does not shrink their cognitive burden.

Recent findings suggest that "Real estate has always recognized the value of a well-maintained home. What we're only beginning to recognize is the value of the work required to maintain it," states Laura Marie Rivera, a gender equity and unpaid labor researcher and host of the "Motherhood Advantage" podcast. "The rise of professional house managers puts a job title and salary on responsibilities that mothers have managed for generations—largely without either.".

Unpaid household work in the U.S. is worth up to $6 trillion a year, and none of it shows up in the GDP. However, the rise of house mangers is finally putting a dollar amount on the mental load of keeping a home operational.

"Paying someone to manage a household doesn't just reveal the economic value of the work, it reveals the scope of the work," says Rivera. "We're not witnessing the invention of a upcoming profession so much as the professional recognition of work that has been hiding in plain sight.".

Sources indicate that the good news is that having a house manager isn't only for the wealthy. In general, cost depends on where you live and what you need the house manager to take on.

It has been revealed that "Families hire and pay house managers directly, and pay ranges from $25 to more than $50 an hour depending on location and scope," says Hubbell. "It doesn't have to be full time: 80% of families start with part-time help, averaging 15 to 20 hours per week.".

It has been revealed that for many families, a house manager can be a more practical investment than several separate kinds of help, because it brings that support together in one role. However, there are still options when budgetary constraints prohibit the employment of a house manager.

According to recent reports, "Support doesn't have to start with a hire," notes Hubbell. "It can begin with mapping out everything it takes to run your home and deciding what to drop, what to share with a partner, and where you need help most.".

That being remarked, for those who can swing it, having a house manager can be life-changing.

In theory this all sounds amazing, but what's it like in practice? We checked in with a house manager and a family that's hired a house manager to get the inside scoop. But the short version is, both are very happy with their decision.

Before becoming a house manager, Terry Boch worked as an executive assistant, but also spent years as a stay-at-home mom raising her three children.

Once they were grown and she reentered the work force, she was enjoying being an executive assistant again but realized she wanted something less computer-focused and more hands-on. That's when she came across a job post seeking house managers. Intrigued, she pursued the opportunity, was matched with a family in New Jersey, and found it was a perfect fit for her skill set.

Sources indicate that "I love transforming an already beautiful house into a warm, welcoming home that looks and smells inviting every day," says Boch, whose primary responsibilities include meal planning, grocery shopping and meal preparation, laundry, resetting bedrooms and living spaces, and plant care. "I work approximately 15–20 hours per week, but I like to say that I get to play house in a home I could never afford.".

In reality, however, Boch notes she sees what she does as much more about creating a home than maintaining a house.

Sources indicate that "Although my interaction with the children is limited, knowing that I can contribute to an environment where they feel comfortable, cared for, and happy brings me tremendous joy," claims Boch. "I love making a home feel welcoming, anticipating what a family needs, and taking pride in all the little things that make everyday life more enjoyable. I'm not a house cleaner; I'm a homemaker at heart.".

On the flip side, Krissel Varela found her way to the idea of hiring a house manager online.

It has been revealed that "Following Sage Haus on social media really opened my eyes to what household support could look like," says Varela. "I had always thought about help in a more traditional sense, like a nanny or someone full-time, but started realizing we could shape the support around what our family actually needed.".

According to recent reports, though she'd had a nanny when her kids were younger and she was working a corporate job, once they reached school age, they didn't need that kind of assistance anymore. However, their lives didn't get less busy.

"Between school, sports, activities, keeping our household running, and now building a business of my own, there are just so many moving pieces," claims Varela. The idea of a house manager made sense for her family, though they didn't need someone full time.

It has been revealed that "Right now, we have help about 8 to 10 hours a week, and even though that's not a huge number of hours, the impact feels so much bigger," says Varela. Her house manager is usually with them on Mondays and Thursdays, with some flexibility predicated on their needs.

"Between laundry, household organization, errands, and all those little tasks that add up throughout the week, having someone share those responsibilities makes such a difference," she adds.

Though it's been only a few months, Varela claims she can already feel a huge life shift.

Recent findings suggest that "It's not just the actual hours saved; it's also the mental space that comes from knowing someone else is helping keep things moving without having to manage every little detail," indicates Varela. "It's also given me more room for the things that are easy to push aside when life gets busy, whether that's spending quality time with my husband, enjoying our weekends, or even having a little time for myself. Having that extra support has really helped me be more intentional about where my time and energy go.".

And that is exactly what a house manager is supposed to do, open up space for life at home to be about more than just getting by every day.

Industry observers note that "People should also know there's a cost to getting support and a cost to going without it, whether that's your health, your relationships, or your connection with your family," says Hubbell. "The goal isn't to outsource your life; it's to get enough support to be present for it.".

Recent findings suggest that asset manager Bitwise has filed an S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash (ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The document appeared in the SEC's database on Nov. 17, 2026. On Wednesday, ZEC rose to $975 before it pulled back to around $927.

Sources indicate that zcash is often called a "more secret" version of Bitcoin. According to the S-1, the Zcash network supports two types of transactions, and the "shielded" ones use a form of zero-knowledge cryptography known as zk-SNARKs. Holders of shielded Zcash "may selectively disclose transaction information to third parties," the filing claims.

Bitwise's fund will not use this feature. "The Trust does not engage in shielded transactions in connection with its activities," according to the document.

According to recent reports, the shares are expected to list on the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) under the ticker ZEC. According to the S-1, Coinbase Custody Trust Organization will act as the Zcash custodian, and BNY Mellon will serve as the cash custodian. Bitwise also wrote that "the Trust will not stake or otherwise seek to derive additional Zcash from its holdings." The sponsor fee in the filing is listed as "0.___% per annum.".

In the risk section of the S-1, Bitwise wrote that "a number of digital asset trading platforms have delisted Zcash, restricted trading in Zcash or declined to support Zcash." According to the filing, many of these platforms cited regulatory or compliance concerns.

Industry observers note that the platforms that still support Zcash "do so only with respect to transparent addresses and do not permit deposits or withdrawals to or from shielded addresses," the document indicates. Bitwise also pointed to new EU rules that take effect on July 10, 2027. According to the S-1, the rules will "prohibit credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in the European Union" from keeping accounts in such assets.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan named Zcash one of his top three assets for the decade in September, alongside Bitcoin and tokenization projects. Three days before the S-1 filing, he called ZEC a "golden mean" between open Bitcoin and anonymous Monero in an interview.

Grayscale's Zcash fund (ZCSH) has traded on NYSE Arca since August 2026, and the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF on Nasdaq in October. ZCSH held $496.79 million as of the Nov. 17 close, according to SoSoValue. The fund has attracted $168.76 million in net inflows since its launch, and it recorded no inflows on Nov. 17, when Bitwise filed its S-1.

Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering important questions about its effects on mental health.
  • Sources indicate that published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition.
  • It has been revealed that the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering important questions about its effects on mental health. A major latest study suggests that people who struggle to control their cannabis use face a substantially greater likelihood of experiencing suicidal thoughts.

Sources indicate that published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition. Despite major shifts in marijuana laws and public attitudes, this troubling association remained remarkably consistent over a decade.

It has been revealed that the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Researchers examined data collected between 2014 and 2023, a period when cannabis became increasingly accessible across the United States.

"What surprised me most was not that cannabis use disorder was associated with suicidal thoughts, but that this association did not appear to strengthen over time," said lead author Tosin Philip Oyetunji, MPH, a doctoral student in public health at the University of California, Merced. "[Yet,] it remains an important mental health concern that deserves attention.".

Cannabis and Suicidal Thoughts Show a Persistent Link.

The connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thinking was observed across different age groups, sexes, and racial and ethnic backgrounds. However, women and younger adults indicated particularly elevated risks.

Importantly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for depression, psychological distress, and other factors that could influence mental health outcomes.

The consistency of the results was especially notable given how dramatically the cannabis landscape has changed. Recreational marijuana is now legal in half of U.S. states, and cannabis products have become increasingly potent. These developments have raised concerns among public health experts about whether broader access might contribute to worsening mental health.

Yet the study offers some reassurance on that particular question. Sidra Goldman-Mellor, PhD, a professor of public health at UC Merced and the study's senior author, noted that the association between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts did not become stronger during the 10 years examined.

Industry observers note that "Suicidal ideation does not seem to have increased among people with cannabis use disorder, despite all this legal and social change," explained Goldman-Mellor. Yet, "people with cannabis use disorder are still at a very substantially increased likelihood of experiencing serious suicidal thoughts, and that's not something that is widely understood.".

Why Cannabis Use Disorder Matters.

The researchers stress that these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that everyone who uses marijuana faces the same elevated risk.

The study focused specifically on cannabis use disorder, a condition in which people have difficulty controlling their marijuana consumption even when it causes problems in their lives. Someone with the disorder may continue using cannabis despite harmful consequences or repeated attempts to cut back.

This distinction is vital because problematic cannabis use differs from occasional or otherwise nonproblematic consumption.

The findings also do not establish that cannabis use disorder directly causes suicidal thoughts. Because the research identified an association rather than a cause-and-effect relationship, it cannot determine whether problematic cannabis use contributes to suicidal thinking, whether underlying mental health difficulties contribute to both conditions, or whether other factors help explain the connection.

Nevertheless, the results point to a significant mental health concern that deserves greater recognition, particularly among people seeking help for problematic cannabis use.

Researchers Urge Greater Mental Health Screening.

One practical implication is that health care professionals should look beyond cannabis consumption itself when evaluating patients with cannabis use disorder.

In a recent development, rather than focusing exclusively on depression or substance use symptoms, clinicians may benefit from asking patients directly about suicidal thoughts as part of a broader mental health assessment. This could help identify people who need additional care but whose struggles might otherwise remain unnoticed.

"Someone seeking help for cannabis use disorder may also be experiencing suicidal thoughts that are not immediately apparent," said Oyetunji. "The goal is not to assume that everyone with cannabis use disorder is suicidal but to identify those who may need additional assessment, treatment, or support.".

According to recent reports, the study arrives at a time when marijuana is increasingly viewed as a relatively low-risk substance. Public perceptions have shifted considerably, and negative attitudes toward cannabis have declined alongside expanding legalization and social acceptance.

However, these changes have not eliminated the mental health challenges associated with cannabis use disorder. Even though the strength of the association with suicidal thoughts did not increase over the study period, the elevated odds remained substantial.

The researchers suggest that health care providers, policymakers, and community organizations can play an vital role by improving awareness, identifying vulnerable individuals, and making appropriate mental health support more accessible.

As attitudes toward marijuana continue to evolve, the findings serve as a reminder that the needs of people experiencing problematic cannabis use should remain a public health priority.

Mentioned Oyetunji, "As cannabis becomes more accessible and socially accepted, we should ensure that the people struggling with its use are not overlooked.".

  • The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.
  • Industry observers note that the independent attestation report was released on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP Ledger (XRPL) has marked a significant step in its journey to institutional adoption by becoming the first public permissionless layer-1 blockchain to see its principles of Architecture and Resiliency independently verified by the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

Industry observers note that the independent attestation report was released on Nov. 13, further strengthening the assertion of XRP Ledger's compliance with institutional financial infrastructure requirements.

This comes at a time when banks and asset managers are increasingly considering blockchain technology to enable tokenization of deposits, stablecoins, investment funds and other financial instruments.

The Global Layer One initiative is a collaborative effort between prominent financial institutions and policymakers to set standards for digital financial infrastructure.

Its main goal is to make cross-border transactions for tokenised assets seamless while ensuring that blockchain networks adhere to internationally expected standards for financial market infrastructure.

The GL1 Market Infrastructure Toolkit assesses blockchain networks for adherence to 10 principles, including governance, legal foundation, settlement finality, architecture, operational resiliency, access, interoperability, and privacy.

Interestingly, XRPLF self-assessed XRPL for all 10 principles.

CertiK independently verified it only for the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

XRPLF also provided details on how requirements specific to private/permissioned networks are addressed by managing related risks for XRPL’s decentralized nature, open-source governance model, and protocol amendments.

XRP Ledger Foundation executive director Brett Mollin emphasized the need to give financial institutions tangible evidence instead of pitching ideas.

Mollin added that independent attestation from CertiK also gives financial institutions more confidence while vetting the network.

It does not mean that XRPL meets all the standards mentioned in the toolkit completely.

The XRP Ledger Foundation will continue to update its assessment in line with the development of GL1 principles and XRPL protocol amendments that are activated.

Nonetheless, it's another step towards XRPL's bid to be a possible infrastructure for regulated financial institutions looking for blockchain-based settlement and tokenization.

The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of Upcoming York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.

It has been revealed that the AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation. With the tech constantly growing and producing newly minted millionaires, the impacts of deep-pocketed AI professionals entering the Fresh York real estate market are just beginning to be felt, agents there say.

There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in Newly introduced York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.

Major AI frontrunners like Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, and EliseAI have opened offices in Upcoming York, contributing to the thriving commercial real estate market.

“It’s been pretty unbelievable, what’s happening in the public sphere of the AI business. We’re seeing a ton of AI leasing activity on the ground in Fresh York,” Evan Kleinberg, co-founder of Cornelia Street Partners, a boutique commercial real estate firm, told Realtor.com. “And it’s been happening so fast, it’s almost representative of the technology itself. The companies hire immediately and they need space yesterday.”.

While Kleinberg has been keeping eyes on the AI industry for the past couple of years, his brokerage worked with its first AI specific firm about 12 months ago, at the end of 2025. Since then, the brokerage has secured leases for five companies developing proprietary AI models.

According to recent reports, there are a number of reasons Kleinberg sees AI companies expanding east and planting roots in New York. The city has fully rebounded from the pandemic and has an attractive lifestyle that draws many young professionals. Plus, companies see the benefit of being close to their portfolio businesses.

It has been revealed that “Ultimately, if your goal is to raise money from Goldman Sachs or JP Morgan or one of the major private equity groups like Apollo, they’re all here,” Kleinberg explained. “So wanting to get close to them is an underlying reason to move.”.

With these fresh offices comes a hoard of young, newly wealthy professionals who are looking to build a home in New York, many of whom are stepping into an already fiercely competitive luxury real estate market.

“Wall Street has historically been a major driver of Manhattan luxury real estate, and now we’re really starting to see the effects of AI. It’s becoming an important engine for wealth creation and housing demand,” Michelle Griffith, a residential real estate agent in Fresh York City, told Realtor.com. “Right now in Manhattan, we are already in a very tight rental market. Even for the last year, rents are up anywhere from 10% to 20% in Manhattan, especially for these luxury properties.”.

Recent findings suggest that as of November, the median sold price of a home in Manhattan is $1,150,000, a 15% year over year increase. Some Manhattan neighborhoods have had more extreme changes.

Sources indicate that the Lower East Side, for example, saw the median sale price jump 28% year over year to $1,435,000. Rent in the Lower East Side also increased 11% year over year, for a median of $5,947 per month.

The Newly introduced York City luxury residential landscape is no stranger to competition, with deep pocketed masses vying for a severely limited inventory of spaces. With the flood of AI professionals, another layer of people has been added to the market.

In a recent development, griffith recalled a recent listing at 50 Gramercy Park North, which had historically rented for $30,000. While a rental like this, which is in the higher end of the market, would previously take 30 to 60 days to identify a tenant, the listing had eight rental bids after 48 hours on the market, with half above asking.

Most workers are determined to live close to work, making it especially challenging to secure an apartment in these highly sought after neighborhoods.

OpenAI’s 90,000-square-foot New York office is located in the Puck Building, which sits on the boarder of SoHo and Nolita in Manhattan.

Anthropic’s New York hub takes up the entirety of a 16-story building at 330 Hudson Street in the Hudson Square neighborhood of Lower Manhattan.

Industry observers note that “The offices are in fantastic locations, so it’s easy to find great housing within walking distance,” said Griffith. “The challenge is finding that apartment because there is very, very limited inventory because those neighborhoods were already popular and in demand.”.

For luxury agents, the challenge is no longer finding tenants with the money to rent high priced rentals, its finding the rentals for deep pocketed tenants.

It has been revealed that when Griffith began in real estate 15 years ago, an apartment for $100,000 per month might be the biggest rental of the year. Now, rentals for $80,000 to even $150,000 are common and moving promptly, she shared.

Sources indicate that the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky.

Sources indicate that the UK's upcoming crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027.

According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection.".

In the letter, HPC also compared public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote.

HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them.

On Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity.".

On Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than new legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time.

Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An international research team has developed a new technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease. In experiments involving mice with Parkinson's-like symptoms, the approach significantly improved movement problems without requiring permanently implanted electrodes.

The technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain. When exposed to an external magnetic field, these particles generate tiny forces that activate nearby nerve cells. Unlike conventional brain stimulation treatments, which rely on surgically implanted electrodes, the new approach uses magnetic forces to influence brain activity. The findings, published in Advanced Science, come from researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), RWTH Aachen, and the Universities of Maastricht (the Netherlands) and Leuven (Belgium).

Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.

Parkinson's disease develops as brain cells responsible for producing dopamine gradually break down. Dopamine is a chemical messenger that plays a vital role in controlling movement. As its levels decline, communication within the brain's movement circuits becomes disrupted, contributing to tremors and other motor difficulties.

For some patients, deep brain stimulation can help control these symptoms. This treatment uses a device known as a brain pacemaker, which is implanted beneath the collarbone and connected to electrodes placed deep inside the brain. The electrodes deliver electrical stimulation to a region called the subthalamic nucleus (STN for short), helping to modify abnormal activity in the brain circuits responsible for movement.

Although this treatment can provide substantial relief, it requires a complex surgical procedure and does not work for everyone.

It has been revealed that "The procedure is relatively complex, however, and not always successful," explains Prof. Dr. Danijela Gregurec from the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy at FAU. "This puts many Parkinson's patients off, and not all patients are suitable candidates for one of these pacemakers.".

The researchers believe magnetic stimulation could eventually provide another option, allowing doctors to influence the same deep brain structures without leaving electrodes permanently implanted.

How Tiny Magnetic Particles Stimulate Brain Cells.

The new technology takes advantage of the ability of certain nerve cells to detect physical pressure and mechanical forces.

Sources indicate that "We use magnetic nanoparticles that we implant in the brain," Gregurec explains. "They have a special shape and a magnetic structure. They were developed in order to transform magnetic fields into tiny mechanical forces.".

Rather than sending electrical pulses directly into the brain, the technique uses these particles to produce extremely small physical movements when a magnetic field is applied.

"The traditional method establishes an electrical connection to the brain," she says. "In contrast, we use the neurons' natural mechanosensors to influence regions deep within the brain.".

Recent findings suggest that the process works by gently changing the shape of nearby nerve cell membranes. Imagine pressing a finger against an inflated balloon and creating a small indentation in its surface. The magnetic particles produce a similar effect on a microscopic scale.

This slight deformation opens specialized channels in the cell membrane that respond to mechanical pressure. Once opened, these channels allow electrically charged particles called ions to enter the nerve cells, changing their electrical activity and providing a way to stimulate the targeted brain circuits.

Magnetic Brain Stimulation Improves Movement in Mice.

It has been revealed that to investigate whether the technology could relieve Parkinson's symptoms, the international research team conducted experiments using mice with damage to the same types of dopamine-producing nerve cells affected by the disease in humans. This damage caused movement difficulties resembling those seen in Parkinson's patients.

It has been revealed that "Together with our partners from Maastricht, we injected magnetic nanoparticles developed here at FAU into the animals' subthalamic nucleus," Gregurec explains. "That is the very region in the brain that is also an important target for conventional deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.".

Sources indicate that the researchers used precise stereotactic injection techniques to deliver the particles to the intended location. These methods rely on carefully calculated three-dimensional coordinates to guide instruments into specific brain structures. Accurate placement was particularly important because the treatment needed to affect the correct neural circuits involved in movement.

After the particles were positioned, the researchers applied an external magnetic field. The results were encouraging: the mice revealed significant improvements in their movement deficits.

"The effect is roughly equivalent to what we would have expected after implanting a brain pacemaker," says Gregurec.

The findings suggest that magnetic nanoparticles could provide a different way to achieve some of the benefits of conventional deep brain stimulation, without the need for permanently implanted electrodes.

Could Future Parkinson's Treatments Use Magnetic Headbands?

Another encouraging finding involved how the brain responded to the implanted particles over time. The magnetic nanoparticles remained in place throughout an observation period lasting several months, and the researchers found no signs of inflammation. This suggests that the particles were well tolerated during the experiments.

However, delivering the particles still required an injection directly into the brain. Gregurec and her colleagues are now investigating ways to make the procedure even less invasive.

One possibility is to develop particles that could be injected into the bloodstream and then travel into the brain by crossing the blood-brain barrier. This protective boundary normally prevents many substances circulating in the blood from entering brain tissue. Finding a way to deliver the particles across it could eliminate the need for direct brain injections.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers are also exploring compact wearable devices capable of generating the magnetic fields needed for stimulation. One possibility is a headband that patients could put on themselves, potentially making treatment more convenient and adjustable.

These ideas remain at an early stage, and the researchers expect that several more years of development will be needed before the technology could be considered for clinical use.

According to recent reports, "Nevertheless, we are convinced that the fresh method has enormous potential," Gregurec states. "It is not only considerably simpler and cheaper than a conventional brain pacemaker, it is probably also more flexible. Adjusting the parameters of the magnetic field would allow us to control the nanoparticles more accurately.".

Beyond its potential medical applications, the technology could also become a valuable scientific tool. By allowing researchers to stimulate nerve cells through carefully controlled mechanical forces, it offers a newly introduced way to explore how physical changes at the cellular level influence brain activity.

Although the treatment has so far been demonstrated only in animals, its ability to improve movement without permanently implanted electrodes represents a promising step toward fresh approaches to Parkinson's disease and brain stimulation.

Breaking: How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets Fresh

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, at first glance, Fresh Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene.
  • Located halfway between New York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents.
  • In Latest Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, at first glance, Fresh Hope, PA, looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene. However, a closer look reveals that the historic borough shares an architectural DNA with Europe's premier capitals.

Located halfway between New York City and Philadelphia, New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents. Yet it boasts an outsized reputation as a beloved regional tourist destination renowned for its art galleries, boutiques, riverside dining, and cultural institutions, led by the iconic Bucks County Playhouse, which has hosted major stars such as Grace Kelly, Robert Redford, and Liza Minnelli.

In Latest Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.

"A lot of the homes around here, especially some of the larger homes, all started off as an old stone farmhouse, so incorporating some of that character while building the major steel and glass additions is very much an architectural vibe that is done here," Nicholas Esser, managing partner at Addison Wolfe Real Estate, tells Realtor.com®.

The market's remarkably varied housing stock also includes stately Colonial and Victorian homes, sprawling legacy estates, and cutting-edge upcoming construction that would not look out of place in the heart of Silicon Valley.

Architect Ralph Fey, with Ralph C. Fey Architects in Doylestown, PA, explains that New Hope's signature look is rooted in regulatory necessity, because more than half of the town falls in a strictly regulated historic district, which rarely allows older buildings to be torn down to make way for new builds.

Rather than viewing zoning laws as a creative roadblock, Fey has made his professional mark by seamlessly merging history with contemporary living.

According to recent reports, "Some of the best architecture is born out of constraints," he tells Realtor.com. "The goal, the fun, the challenge is how to maintain that historic feel, meet the guidelines of the historic district, but provide the amenities that we now want to have as we live on the water.".

Industry observers note that maureen Reynolds, a Serhant luxury real estate agent in Newly introduced Hope, counts herself among Fey's clients. She right now lives in an 1832-built converted horse barn with tall ceilings and hand-hewn beams.

"I have all the modern amenities because of Ralph," she tells Realtor.com.

While Fresh Hope lacks the urban density and wealth of major metros, Fey claims, its architectural style "is more like London, where you have newer construction next to historic construction, next to really historic construction, and it is that fabric that makes London so exciting.".

Founded in the 18th century on the banks of the Delaware River, Fresh Hope was previously called Wells Ferry and later Coryell’s Ferry.

The borough was rechristened after a fire in 1790 destroyed several mills owned by local businessman Benjamin Parry. He rebuilt them as the New Hope Mills, inspiring the town’s optimistic new name.

By the late 19th century, New Hope had gained a reputation as an art colony and emerged as a major hub for American and Pennsylvania Impressionists, including William Langson Lathrop, Edward Willis Redfield, and Daniel Garber.

It has been revealed that "Upcoming Hope definitely has an architectural richness that's been developed over centuries," says Reynolds. "Its historic buildings' relationship to the river and surrounding landscape give it a character that cannot be created overnight. And the challenge and opportunity for the architects, for Realtors®, and for developers is to respect that history while designing homes that accommodate the way people live today.".

Fey agrees, maintaining that Newly introduced Hope's success as a thriving housing market is rooted in its past and the borough's fierce commitment to protecting it.

"The same little river town 5 miles down the road that did not have a historic district, where all the homes were knocked down, would not have that feel of a classic historic town, and would not have that charm, and it could potentially lose it," he indicates. "It's really vital to us as architects to preserve that feeling, and that's part of the reason why Newly introduced Hope is as prized and treasured as it is—it's for its history.".

Even with newly introduced construction, a premium is placed on designing in harmony with the town.

Fey and Reynolds frequently work with clients to select natural building materials such as locally sourced stone, cedar wood, and slate roof tiles. They complement surrounding centuries-old structures rather than clashing with the local aesthetic.

Industry observers note that "Most of my clients are very in love with the feel of the historic Latest Hope and also would like to see some of the amenities of slightly more glass, slightly higher ceilings," notes the architect. "So when we are doing additions on the traditional homes or existing historic housing stock, our goal is to contribute to the street.".

Industry observers note that despite its modest size, Latest Hope commands an impressively broad appeal. Esser and Fey say buyers range from locals looking to upgrade or build their dream homes to affluent transplants from neighboring New York, Philadelphia, and New Jersey hunting for a primary residence or weekend pied-à-terre, alongside retirees drawn to Pennsylvania's favorable tax climate.

Some home shoppers, however, come from much farther afield.

Reynolds’ roster of New Hope clients includes buyers from the South of France, Sweden, Canada, and Japan, cementing the town’s status as a market punching well above its weight.

Industry observers note that in August, the Philadelphia Business Journal ranked Fresh Hope as the nation's No. 2 hottest luxury housing market during the second quarter of 2026 among 327 markets analyzed.

"That's an extraordinary distinction for a community of this size," notes Reynolds.

Industry observers note that prices have surged accordingly. Reynolds recounts how townhomes originally priced between $1.4 million and $1.8 million jumped to $2 million–$3.2 million in less than three years.

The latest Realtor.com housing data indicates that in October, the median listing price in Newly introduced Hope topped $2 million, up more than 27% from a year ago.

Meanwhile, the luxury-tier threshold—representing the top 10% of the market—was just over $5 million.

While inventory was up more than 50% year over year last month, Realtor.com senior economist Hannah Jones notes that supply still remains nearly 60% below pre-pandemic levels.

“Demand comes largely from cash-rich buyers in the surrounding region, including a growing share from Upcoming Jersey alongside the New York metro, who are insulated from mortgage rates hovering around 7%,” she says.

As always with real estate, location remains paramount.

"If I have something on the river, it usually sells within a couple days, and that can be something, too, that is not turnkey—we're talking about something that can be slightly a shell inside," claims Reynolds.

Ultimately, what keeps buyers flocking to New Hope from near and far is the sheer architectural variety packed into the pint-sized, picture-perfect historic borough.

"The beautiful thing around here is that there's gorgeous properties everywhere, and the home styles do change between the more modern construction, with the beams and 12-foot ceilings, and old stone construction, but they mesh really well," concludes Esser.

Snejana Farberov is a reporter at Realtor.com covering the U.S. housing market and the latest domestic real estate trends. She has worked as a general assignment journalist in New York City and Long Island for 16 years, writing for New York Post, Daily Mail, and News 12. Snejana earned bachelor's degrees in journalism and Italian from St. John's University, followed by a master’s degree from Columbia University School of Journalism.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.
  • To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.
  • Studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control. These drugs also influence biological processes involved in brain function, raising questions about whether they could help preserve memory and thinking abilities.

To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.

Studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory. However, research involving humans has produced less consistent findings. Analyses of patient health records have found an association between GLP-1 treatment and a reduced risk of dementia among people with type 2 diabetes. These observational findings are encouraging, but they cannot determine whether the medications themselves are responsible for the lower risk.

More definitive results have also raised questions. In Novo Nordisk's EVOKE and EVOKE+ clinical trials, semaglutide failed to slow the progression of early Alzheimer's disease. Although the treatment affected several biological markers associated with Alzheimer's, those changes did not translate into a measurable slowing of the disease.

Why Weight Loss Drugs May Still Benefit the Brain.

Despite the disappointing Alzheimer's results, researchers believe GLP-1 medications could still offer cognitive benefits to certain groups of patients.

Sources indicate that people living with obesity or type 2 diabetes sometimes experience difficulties with attention, planning, and the speed at which they process information. These cognitive problems are often associated with metabolic health and blood vessel function, suggesting they may respond differently to treatment than the changes caused by Alzheimer's disease.

Improving blood sugar regulation, metabolism, or vascular health could potentially help preserve cognitive abilities, even if the same medications cannot slow an established neurodegenerative disease.

Stina Börchers, the review's first author and a researcher affiliated with both the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen, emphasizes the need to determine whether starting treatment earlier could make a difference.

"We need to find out whether these treatments can help people with obesity or diabetes preserve their cognitive abilities, particularly if treatment begins before cognitive problems become established. It is also important to identify which patients might benefit," notes Stina Börchers.

Unlocking Upcoming Treatments to Protect Memory.

A central unanswered question is how GLP-1 medications might influence the brain. Their potential cognitive effects could result from improvements in metabolic health, direct actions within the brain, or a combination of both.

Understanding these mechanisms could help researchers identify which patients are most likely to benefit and potentially lead to medications designed specifically to support memory and other thinking abilities.

Christoffer Clemmensen, the review's senior author and a research group leader at the University of Copenhagen, sees an opportunity to use increasingly advanced obesity treatments to explore the connection between metabolism and the brain.

Sources indicate that "Obesity medicines are becoming increasingly sophisticated, offering fresh opportunities to understand how metabolic regulation influences brain function. By disentangling the direct and indirect effects of these drugs on the brain, we may ultimately be able to develop treatments specifically aimed at preserving cognitive function," notes Christoffer Clemmensen.

According to recent reports, the researchers are calling for clinical trials that evaluate memory, attention, and other cognitive abilities beginning when patients first start treatment. Following these changes over time could help establish whether GLP-1 drugs genuinely protect brain function and clarify who might benefit most.

They also stress that treatment is not without potential drawbacks, particularly for older adults and people who are physically frail. Rapid weight loss can lead to a reduction in muscle mass, which may weaken physical function and offset some of the possible benefits.

Careful monitoring will therefore be essential as researchers investigate whether today's weight loss and diabetes medications could eventually provide new ways to protect the brain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

California-born sculptor Chester Beach worked out of a Fresh York City studio between 1907 and 1952, nabbing high-profile commissions from the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, as well as the 1928 Summer Olympics.

But, like many artists, he carved out space for a pastoral retreat away from the hustle and bustle.

In 1917, after living in Rome for a brief period, he and his wife, Eleanor Beach, established a home in Brewster, NY, in Putnam County, just 55 miles north of the city. They named the Arts & Crafts-style estate OldWalls.

Now these 10.49 acres—including four buildings, comprising a compound—is looking for a upcoming steward.

"There have only been three owners including the original family that owned it up until 2009," says listing agent Will Stuart, of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Upcoming England Properties. "My sellers have been there for two years.".

Listing for $4,150,000, the latest owner won't be the first to seek a deeper connection to nature while still being close to Manhattan.

Stuart notes that this eight-bedroom, 6.5-bath spread is exceptionally tied to its origins.

"Each owner has become a steward of the property and has preserved extensive family photographs, memoirs and documents, and have really kept the story going, which is rare with these kinds of properties," he indicates. "A lot of times the information gets lost along the way. The story has been preserved so well.".

The estate includes a four-bedroom stone residence with plaster walls, hand-crafted stonework and stained glass. There’s also a separate guest studio with a kitchen, bath, sleeping loft and stone fireplace. And, a two-bedroom guest cottage dating back to the 1940s with cozy amenities such as a fireplace and screened-in porch.

Another way the property has been preserved is through art the original owners brought into the house.

Tiles collected from Spain, Guatemala and Italy are laid into the floor, says Stuart. He adds that "there’s actually a cluster of Roman floor tiles under the dining-room table.".

The kitchen’s chandelier was born out of a turntable Beach used for sculpting. Eleanor’s bird paintings (112 in all) are incorporated into the living room’s ceiling.

It has been revealed that “There’s three outbuildings in addition to the main residence that all offer incredible living space and charm,” notes Stuart. “Each one of them has a story and a history.”.

For example, in the detached studio, which was built before the home, are many of Beach’s tools and hardware, as well as the original doors.

A buyer drawn to that history is who Stuart is courting. But it could also be an equestrian, as the property features a five-stall barn with a spacious one-bedroom apartment. Nearby are run-outs, rolling grass turnout paddocks, a riding field with access to trails, and a riding arena in the sand.

According to recent reports, “We have a lot of equestrians that have moved into the community,” states Stuart. “A lot of the equestrian people travel to Florida in the winter so they’re here half the year, but most people are here year-round.” Two miles down the road is Old Salem Farm, a 120-acre boarding and training facility.

Above all, the buyer will likely be someone who likes to be near Manhattan but also have a countryside retreat, just like Beach once did.

In a recent development, this mirrors a trend Stuart continues to see among buyers. “People looking for more space, more privacy, but want to stay within close proximity to the city,” he says. “This is a real compound here. It’s someone who is hosting family or guests.”.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (363 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and issue unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.
  • According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and problem Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.
  • Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and issue unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.

According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and problem Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.

Combined, the total value of the affected assets stood at around $1.06 million, per Onchain Lens.

Following the hack, the funds were transferred through the decentralized exchange Uniswap and multiple crypto wallets, making it challenging to trace their final destination.

Sources indicate that the attack targeted Gonka AI's cross-chain bridge. The cross-chain bridge makes it possible to transfer assets from Gonka AI's native chain to Ethereum and vice versa.

According to the project's technical documentation, withdrawing funds from Gonka to Ethereum requires certain cryptographic signatures from the network's validator set.

The cryptographic signatures are checked against the BLS group key, which changes with every network epoch.

Per the report, the attacker was able to change the epoch BLS group key on the bridge, making it possible for the hacker to control the part of the bridge responsible for authorizing fund withdrawals.

Thus, the hacker was able to withdraw funds from the bridge's stablecoin reserves and issue WGNK tokens without locking the required amount of assets on the native blockchain.

Blockchain security firm Blockaid noted that the hack had taken place, with the total amount of funds stolen reaching about $1.05 million across roughly five transactions at the time of the initial alert.

At the time it spotted the suspicious activity, Blockaid noted that the hack was still ongoing.

Onchain Lens's numbers differ slightly, with the firm reporting around $884,800 in stablecoin withdrawals and $172,000 in unbacked WGNK issuance.

Notably, the issuance of unbacked tokens presents an additional problem, given that such tokens could potentially enter circulation without the necessary reserves to back them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.
  • In his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov.
  • The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.

In his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov. 18 notice issued by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC). The notice urges rental car services to be cautious about unnecessarily storing images of driver’s licenses and other government-issued identification documents.

The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.

Sources indicate that the incident began when the company noticed suspicious activity on its system on Sept. 25. As a result, it launched an investigation into whether someone had accessed its systems without permission, potentially exposing customer data.

As per the disclosure by Park24 on Oct. 23, about 6.63 million customer accounts were impacted by the breach.

Worse, the investigation uncovered evidence that hackers had transmitted 1,464,800 encrypted images of identification documents, including driver’s licenses, to external locations.

Besides that, another 891,602 encrypted images of identification documents were accessed suspiciously. However, investigators found no evidence that these additional ID images had been transmitted outside the company’s systems.

It has been revealed that japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission issued its notice on Nov. 18, focusing on the risks of retaining sensitive personal data even after its original purpose has been fulfilled.

The regulatory body stressed that storing unnecessary identification images could significantly worsen the consequences of cyberattacks.

Although Japan’s latest warning specifically targets the rental car industry, CZ’s decision to share his concerns about this glitch also raises questions about personal data protection in the crypto industry.

Generally, centralized crypto exchanges require users to go through a Know Your Customer (KYC) process to access their trading platforms.

Depending on the platform and jurisdiction, these processes may require users to provide photos of their passports, driver’s licenses, national ID cards, and other sensitive information.

This kind of sensitive data can be a goldmine for cybercriminals, who can exploit stolen personal information for various activities such as identity theft, phishing attacks, fraudulent registrations, and more.
