📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A sprawling 8,300-square-foot hand-hewn log home on 22 wooded acres in Greenacres, WA has hit the market for under $3 million after a $320,000 price drop.

Built with full timber walls throughout and soaring views of the Pacific Northwest skyline, the seven-bedroom estate offers total seclusion just 15 minutes from the highway.

“It's huge. It's a 8,300-square-foot log cabin and the architecture on this one is just stunning. It's hand-hewn logs,” claims listing agent Denay Hornberger with Realty One Group Eclipse. “It’s a one-of-a-kind property and the owners added a bunch of beautiful features to it.”.

Completed in 2008, the sellers bought the place before it was completed and finished the construction.

“When they first bought it, the builder had spent too much money building it and ended up having to sell it when it was half done. They came in and finished it and added hundreds of thousands of dollars to this property to make it what it is today.” Hornberger explains, adding she lives on an adjacent property. “With the money that's been put into it, [the sellers have] an eye for detail. I mean, everything about this home has been well thought out.”.

Now the owners are listing it for $2.875 million.

Sources indicate that “The thing about a property like this is trying to figure out exactly how to price it because there are no comps to really help you decide where the price is right,” she says, adding the initial asking price was a bit high. “I think we're now right in the sweet spot of where we need to be.”.

The home has seven bedrooms and seven bathrooms with real logs visible almost everywhere.

It has been revealed that “There are similar log cabins but they're not fully log cabins the way that [this home] is. Sometimes you have little bits of logs and then you have drywall,” Hornberger states. “Here, the logs are everywhere throughout the house and that is extremely unique to have that. You feel like you are in a log cabin in every almost every single room you're in.”.

The fact the sellers spared no expense is evident immediately.

“You walk in and your breath is just taken away. It is so beautiful and it's so grand that when you walk in, you just have to take a moment and appreciate it because the windows are huge, the logs are huge,” she claims. “The fireplace is absolutely stunning, and then you look out the window to just woods and skyline. It's just stunning.”.

The home sits on 22-acres of land and while it seems far away from civilization, it isn’t.

“You're actually 15 minutes from the freeway and you're about 20 minutes from the mall,” Hornberger indicates. “So even though you feel like you're in the middle of nowhere, you just drive a little bit and you're back in the mix of things. So, you get the best of both worlds.”.

It also epitomizes the feel of the Pacific Northwest.

In a recent development, “We have that woodsy feel. People like to wear their flannel here and we're kind of a laid-back community,” she explains. “So [the house] is taking the best of the Pacific Northwest and having that cabin-in-the-woodsy feel, which is what we're known for.”.

The amount of land makes it perfect for outdoors activities like hiking and hunting, but the house is also luxurious, meaning two types of perfect buyers.

“If you just want to be outside, it’s a perfect home for that,” Hornberger says. “I think the second perfect buyer is somebody who wants a second home... who's in a hustle and bustle all the time but really wants that getaway that they can go to several times a year, have that peace and quiet from the city, get back to nature, and then go back to their regular lives at the end of the day.”.

Industry News: Can AI Hack Smart Contracts? How AI Agents Are Changing Blockchain Security

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: U

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns.
  • According to recent reports, for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period.
  • To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns. However, because an AI agent can iterate and make use of dependencies, local blockchain forks, and decompilation, it weakens the protection gained by keeping source code secret, and can attempt attacks against complex vulnerabilities such as access control bugs, accounting errors, oracle-related bugs and unexpected contract interactions.

According to recent reports, for example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period. They were able to reproduce exploits for 207 contracts, totalling $550.1 million (simulated stolen funds).

To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).

Finally, they analysed 2,849 recent smart contracts with no known concerns, discovering two previously unknown vulnerabilities that could have resulted in $3,694 (simulated stolen funds), emphasising the ability of AI agents to discover newly introduced vulnerabilities rather than simply exploiting known ones.

Sources indicate that anthropic emphasised that no actual funds were lost during these experiments. It should also be noted that in one of their experiments using GPT-5, it cost $3,476 for API usage, which leaves a slim (simulated) profit.

With automated hacking becoming more effective, how can we be sure that DeFi will be able to stay ahead of these AI agents? Hacken, a blockchain security firm, reported that $1.18 billion was lost in 107 crypto hacks during the third quarter of 2026. 48% of this was from exploiting smart contracts.

Of course, this doesn’t specify the cause of these hacks. Regardless, it emphasises the importance of being able to stay ahead of AIs which could be used for exploitation.

Chainalysis estimates that approximately $36.7 million was stolen in 2026 from DeFi protocols that had not undergone smart contract verification. It also notes AI-assisted reverse engineering as an emerging risk without attributing any particular thefts to AI.

Recent findings suggest that in an experiment by a16z on 20 past DeFi price manipulation exploits, apparent success rates of 50% were reduced to 10% when the researchers restricted access to transactional data that revealed the original exploit. When the researchers gave the AI some high-level information about the DeFi domain, success rates jumped to 70%.

In February 2026, OpenAI and Paradigm released a benchmark for evaluating agents’ abilities in the domains of vulnerability detection, patching, and exploitation using an EVM environment (EVMbench). Results revealed that GPT-5.3-Codex achieved a 71% success rate in exploitation (limited to a sandboxed environment) and 33.3% for GPT-5.

In a recent development, in October 2026, CyberChainBench was released, analyzing 541 exploit events across 9 Ethereum-compatible blockchains. The best-performing configuration achieved 37.5%, 43.7%, and 23.4% success rates for detection, exploitation, and patching respectively.

In a simulation, the best-performing agent profited $57.4 million from exploits on 200 exploit events that occurred after the cutoff. Some of the reported high-severity concerns were evaluated and determined to not be exploitable by OpenZeppelin. Since much of the data is trained on in the public, results may be exaggerated.

Agents will continue to improve, and while current results are not an indication that AI-driven agents are responsible for large scale on-chain thefts, it is an indication that AI can find and exploit weaknesses in smart contracts given a certain environment. Given the ease with which agents can try attacking many different protocols, smaller protocols may see an uptick in exploit attempts.

According to recent reports, teams that implement rigorous testing and monitoring could have an edge over other teams. For example, AI could be used to test a contract prior to deployment, generate regression tests, and identify weird behavior on-chain. A human would still need to verify any potential issues and sign off on changes.

Teams should continue to perform third-party audits and implement other security best practices such as limiting access to sensitive information, setting up alerts and response plans, restricting the amount of money in a wallet, making sure AI systems do not have permissions to transact without human oversight where necessary, and so on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that luxury real estate developers are always looking for newly introduced ways to appeal to potential buyers, with resident amenities—from wellness centers to bowling alleys to sports courts—becoming commonplace. The latest offering? A private glam room.

The Greenwich, a lavish 88-story tower in New York City’s Financial District, landed on the feature as a way to give residents the ultimate luxury—a little more wiggle room in their schedule.

“From the start, we’ve looked for ways to make life easier for our residents and set The Greenwich apart from other condominium buildings,” developer Gregory Davis, Director at Fortress Investment Group, tells Realtor.com®.

In a recent development, “When we thought about who our residents would be and how they live, time stood out as the ultimate luxury. An in-building beauty room offering nail and hair services was a natural fit,” Davis continues.

Residents reportedly book the salon’s services weekly, with benefits ranging from quick touch-ups for meetings to full glam ahead of a gala or special occasion. The building leverages a concierge partner, LIVunLtd, to make sure scheduling is a breeze.

“It’s a popular and convenient amenity, particularly for those who appreciate having access to beauty and wellness services without leaving the building,” Davis adds.

Recent findings suggest that an extra perk? The salon sits on the 86th floor, 800 feet above the city, so residents can enjoy stellar views while they get primped.

Industry observers note that at The Greenwich, the salon is exclusively accessible to residents. The space also includes two private treatment rooms that can accommodate services such as esthetics and massage therapy.

The amenity doesn’t function exactly like a typical salon. Residents can reserve the space, or a treatment room, at no added cost and bring in their own preferred stylists. But for those who don’t have a makeup artist on speed dial, the aforementioned concierge partner can be used to book professionals through a “curated network of independent beauty and wellness providers with a range of specialities.”.

This approach seems to be preferred over having a dedicated glam squad on staff.

“Our residents are sophisticated Newly introduced Yorkers who travel frequently and are often very familiar with the latest beauty and wellness trends,” Davis adds. “Many have specific preferences, whether that means organic products, a stylist experienced with extensions, or a technician specializing in Russian manicures.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s not simply about booking a manicure,” he continues. “It’s about understanding what someone is looking for and finding the right professional to deliver it. When residents aren’t quite sure what they want, we’re happy to make recommendations and introduce them to providers they might not otherwise discover.”.

On that note, pricing is dependent on the provider and service.

It has been revealed that so far, manicures, pedicures, and blowouts have been the most popular uses of the salon. Residents have also booked the treatment rooms for lash technicians and estheticians who offer facials.

Soon, residents will be able to easily access cosmetic injectables.

“We’re currently developing a partnership with Bel Angé Medical Spa in Tribeca to bring a Botox pop-up experience directly to the building,” Davis reveals.

Sources indicate that the salon has become a useful spot for the building, which occasionally hosts resident events. In June, a “Sip and Style” party invited those who live in the building to head to the 86th floor for rosé, light bites, and professional dry hair styling.

In a recent development, “We were especially delighted by the lively mix of men and women who attended. It was a lovely opportunity for residents to connect while enjoying something a little different,” Davis says. “We love being able to bring these kinds of experiences into the building and give residents access to wonderful local partners without ever having to leave home.”.

The Greenwich seems to be ahead of an emerging trend, with a number of upcoming luxury towers looking to offer residents similar amenities, too.

Three upcoming luxury developments in Miami will soon offer salon suites as part of the amenity package, including Bentley Residences, the Perigon Miami Beach, and Fouquet’s Hotel and Residences Miami.

XRP Flashes Biggest Volatility Warning Among Major Cryptocurrencies

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data.
  • Sources indicate that XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median.
  • XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data. The options market indicates that traders are now preparing for price swings that could be nearly double XRP's historical seven-day price move.

Sources indicate that XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median. This figure far exceeds similar metrics for major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Solana (SOL).

XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility. Solana shows the lowest premium among these four cryptocurrencies, Coinbase remarked.

According to recent reports, as the chart below indicates, the options-implied seven-day price move for XRP is around 9.6%, according to Glassnode and Coinbase data as of Nov. 17. This compares to its historical median absolute price move of about 4.9%.

Basically, this means that the options market is signaling a price swing nearly twice as large as XRP's typical seven-day price movement.

It has been revealed that interestingly, Solana's implied price move is also close to 9.5%, almost the same as XRP's. Yet its historical median weekly price move is much higher at about 6.5%.

The key here is that although both cryptocurrencies exhibit similarly large potential price moves, the magnitude of the expected volatility surprise is significantly greater for XRP relative to its usual trading range.

Recent findings suggest that for comparison, Bitcoin shows an options-implied seven-day move of about 6%, versus its historical median of about 3.5%. For Ethereum, these numbers are about 8% and 5.1%, respectively.

Obviously, this latest figure doesn't necessarily imply that XRP is going to crash. It's a sign that options traders expect a major price move regardless of its direction.

In a recent development, implied volatility is a forward-looking measure. It's based on options prices. The higher the implied volatility, the more traders pay for exposure to potential price movements or protection against them.

The chart from Coinbase is based on a one-standard-deviation estimate. It's derived by converting annualized at-the-money implied volatility into a seven-day timeframe.

For XRP, the roughly 9.6% implied move represents a statistical range. It's not a guaranteed price target. A one-standard-deviation range suggests about a 68% chance of the price staying within this range under typical modeling assumptions.

Thus, the latest figure of 1.94x implies that XRP's volatility premium remains high despite a slight decrease from the previous reading.

According to recent reports, from XRP traders' perspective, this can be a very challenging market environment. For traders using leverage, there could be a high risk of liquidation due to potentially sharp price moves.

In a recent development, ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse mentioned on Nov. 19 that crypto markets could rally after Anthropic's IPO, as they did after SpaceX went public. He spoke to CNBC on the day Anthropic's shares started trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

According to Garlinghouse, investors sold Bitcoin and XRP before the listing to free up cash for shares of the Claude developer.

Recent findings suggest that "We talked earlier about the most recent sell-off in the crypto markets — we also saw a sell-off very similar when SpaceX went public. What happens is you've got risk-on assets and people are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO. What we saw after the SpaceX IPO was a rally in the crypto markets. I think you'll see that happen here as well," the Ripple CEO remarked.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the initial range of $70 to $78. The company and its seven co-founders sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million shares they planned to sell earlier. The offering raised $81.3 billion, and a $26 billion private placement brought the total to $107.3 billion.

It has been revealed that at a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, Anthropic became the world's 12th-biggest company, just behind Tesla. SpaceX raised $75 billion in its market debut in June.

Industry observers note that dan Ives of Yorkville Ives stated that "Anthropic's IPO is a massive near-term win for the tech sector." University of Florida finance professor Jay Ritter compared AI with the early internet. "Thirty years ago, the internet was the next big thing. It has changed our lives. Today, artificial intelligence is the next big thing. It will change our lives, too," Ritter said.

Industry observers note that asked about the listing itself, Garlinghouse said that Anthropic's shares would trade well. "I think it's gonna be extremely well received, and we obviously saw a price above the range they had. I think it's gonna trade very well," he said.

In the same interview, Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he said.

Recent findings suggest that after the SpaceX IPO in June, Bitcoin took almost three weeks to turn higher. It started to rise after the U.S. Treasury announced that it would buy back government bonds.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin is facing increased fear and panic among traders as its price volatility continues to intensify, causing both retail and institutional investors to move with caution.
  • While Bitcoin is still struggling to regain momentum amid the persistent market downturn, the latest on-chain data from CryptoQuant shows that Bitcoin's demand has dropped to its weakest level in 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin is facing increased fear and panic among traders as its price volatility continues to intensify, causing both retail and institutional investors to move with caution.

While Bitcoin is still struggling to regain momentum amid the persistent market downturn, the latest on-chain data from CryptoQuant shows that Bitcoin's demand has dropped to its weakest level in 2026.

The data highlights that Bitcoin's apparent demand is rapidly showing signs of weakness, with the metric dropping below -290,000 BTC before seeing a brief recovery to about -255,000 BTC as of November 18.

However, this does not provide any relief, as Bitcoin’s apparent demand remains substantially below its monthly average of around -172,000 BTC.

Recent findings suggest that as such, it appears that investors’ interest in accumulating Bitcoin remains significantly subdued by the fear of potential losses. Hence, investors are growing increasingly cautious about entering the market amid the rising selling pressure.

The data shows that investors are growing increasingly wary of their Bitcoin positions amid growing uncertainty about its potential price movements, as Bitcoin’s price downturn has only intensified over the past few days.

While the asset’s price has dipped further, Bitcoin has suddenly retested $62,000 as of November 18, a price level last seen during the severe price crash in July.

Nonetheless, further data shows that it has briefly recovered to $63,817.43 as of the time of writing, showing a decline of about 1.12% over the past 24 hours.

Despite Bitcoin’s extremely negative demand and weak price movements, market analysts are still positive about a potential reversal, describing the moment as an opportunity to buy at a lower price.

It has been previously observed that while many investors are becoming increasingly bearish, periods of widespread fear can sometimes flush out weaker hands, thereby triggering a change in market direction.

Upcoming Development in the Heart of Florida Equestrian Country Targets Horse Lovers With Farm Lots and Bridle Paths

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced masterplanned community in the heart of Palm Beach County's equestrian country has opened sales to wealthy horse lovers.
  • The Wellington, a private club community in the Village of Wellington, sitting about 16 miles east of West Palm Beach, will cater to the horsey set.
  • It has been revealed that the 253-unit masterplanned community—with estate homes starting at $11 million and townhomes at $6.8 million—will also feature an 18-hole link-style championship golf course designed by Scottish golf course architect David McLay Kidd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced masterplanned community in the heart of Palm Beach County's equestrian country has opened sales to wealthy horse lovers.

The Wellington, a private club community in the Village of Wellington, sitting about 16 miles east of West Palm Beach, will cater to the horsey set.

It has been revealed that the 253-unit masterplanned community—with estate homes starting at $11 million and townhomes at $6.8 million—will also feature an 18-hole link-style championship golf course designed by Scottish golf course architect David McLay Kidd. The median list price in the surrounding area is $849,900, a 12% increase over last year.

But the fresh community will distinguish itself from the luxury development pack with high-end equestrian villas and farm lots, along with a bridle path connecting to the premiere equestrian venue, Wellington International Showgrounds.

Developer Wellington Lifestyle Partners poured capital into improving the show grounds, adding 100 acres and erecting latest competition rings, a covered riding arena, a grass derby field, and stabling that's designed to prioritize ventilation, horse welfare, and rider comfort.

The improvements are expected to encourage exhibitors to arrive earlier in the fall and stay longer into the spring and summer, reinforcing the village's equestrian ecosystem, which pumps about $600 million annually into the local economy, according to the county.

The 400-acre gated community, which won't be fully completed for at least seven years, has four major sections—North, South, Golf Course, and Marketplace.

It has been revealed that the first phase of the project has 49 completed estate homes on lots up to an acre, and sales began in September. (The full build-out is expected by early 2029.).

Home styles are divided into modern, transitional, and classical, with some homes offering waterfront views of football-field-sized human-made lakes.

Estates range from four to eight bedrooms, with each estate boasting a private pool and landscaped grounds. With designs by architects D. Stanley Dixon, Geoffrey Mouen Architects, Morris Adjmi Architects, and Squire & Partners, the community will be managed by Nexus Luxury Collection.

The second phase of the development, Wellington South, will have approximately 100 homes on 175 acres, with five small farms featuring a barn and paddocks.

"These will be very coveted because they will be close to the show grounds," Douglas McMahon, CEO of Wellington Lifestyle Partners and senior managing partner of Nexus Luxury Collection, tells Realtor.com®.

"So much of Wellington is, 'How close do you live to the show grounds?' That's desirable. Almost how you think about a ski town, people want to live near the ski mountain.".

The south portion of the development will have top-notch equestrian facilities, including competition rings, a stadium ring, a derby field, and a covered arena, as well as hundreds of stables. (There are thousands of stables and barns in the greater Wellington village and Palm Beach County.).

Beyond the home estates, there will also be 47 two-story townhomes with private back gardens and swimming pools, in addition to mudrooms for "equestrians and their gear.".

The community's amenity suite will feature private dining; resort-style pools; a fitness center with racquet campus offering tennis, padel, and pickleball; a Purple Dragon club for children; and a main clubhouse and a separate golf clubhouse.

HOA fees are about $1,250 a month, plus $35,000 in annual dues for both clubs for a family. (You do not have to join the clubs.) Like most private clubs, membership is by invitation only.

"We meet everybody," says McMahon. "But we have one rule: Be respectful of everyone and everything.".

Incorporated in 1995, the Village of Wellington, also known as "The Winter Equestrian Capital of the World," is one of the most famed equestrian enclaves in the world.

With nearly half of its 20,000 acres zoned for equestrian pursuits, the area contains over 100 miles of public and private bridle trails, 70 polo fields, and venues for dressage (orchestrated routines set to music) and hunter/jumper activities. There are also 800 noncompetitive farms.

Industry observers note that "If you look at Wellington," notes McMahon. "It's really a tale of two communities.".

There is the year-round community of around 23,000 households; then there is the winter equestrian community stretching from January to mid-April. This swells the local population with about 500,000 spectators and 15,000 horses, flown and trucked in from around the world, and 8,000 riders representing 55 countries.

In a recent development, it's this passionate, horse-loving audience that the development expects to attract to its latest gated haven. But the developer stresses that The Wellington will appeal to others as well—such as residents who may prefer a round of golf or game of padel.

Recent findings suggest that "People might want to cheer their mom or sister on [in horse pursuits], but when they're not doing that, they have other things to do," McMahon notes. "We're appealing to the whole household, whether you're equestrian or not.".

While commercial activity is severely restricted within the equestrian zoning overlay, just outside of it, the new community will offer an 18-acre marketplace with an 80-room luxury boutique hotel and plenty of retail and office space.

"Nothing wrong with a shopping center, but we're trying to create something with more feeling," the developer notes. "Something with a sense of place and purpose.".

The marketplace area will also eventually house 89 residential condos at significantly lower prices than the rest of the community.

The Wellington isn't the only major development happening within the village—billionaire real estate developer Steve Ross is in the midst of building a K-12 school and a 33-acre mixed-used site.

While many buyers within the community will have homes elsewhere, coming down mostly to participate in the horse season, McMahon says that since the COVID-19 pandemic, the area sees just as many people making the enclave their primary home.

"Once one is a horse family, it becomes a big part of the family's life," he adds. "The Wellington is our attempt to create a idealized version of the wonderful lifestyle that is unique and historic in Wellington.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

It has been revealed that the network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed owners on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

Sources indicate that in 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and unveiled their farewell.

In a recent development, the 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an issue we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of latest technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

Industry observers note that however, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

In a recent development, 2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

Industry observers note that in 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

It has been revealed that options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI.

Industry observers note that this suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

Industry observers note that according to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

Sources indicate that at the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history says more than its current price action does.

Sources indicate that XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

It has been revealed that in the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tucked away along Pine Log Creek in Fairmount, GA, sits a nearly 71-acre historic estate that feels less like a residential listing and more like a Hollywood set.
  • Known as Yarborough Mill, the $7 million property features a restored late-1800s Queen Anne Victorian—a 4,500-square-foot former grist mill and plenty of period charm.
  • According to recent reports, "It looks like something that belongs in 'Practical Magic'," says listing agent Logan Fitts with Mountain Sotheby's International Realty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tucked away along Pine Log Creek in Fairmount, GA, sits a nearly 71-acre historic estate that feels less like a residential listing and more like a Hollywood set.

Known as Yarborough Mill, the $7 million property features a restored late-1800s Queen Anne Victorian—a 4,500-square-foot former grist mill and plenty of period charm.

According to recent reports, "It looks like something that belongs in 'Practical Magic'," says listing agent Logan Fitts with Mountain Sotheby's International Realty. “It is definitely the most historic property I've had the chance to work with, and with that it is just so unique.”.

The property has several structures, but the highlights are the former grist mill and a late 1800s Queen Anne Victorian.

Sources indicate that “Everything's original, but it's all been restored because it was not in perfect condition when [the sellers] bought it. It's a complete restore project and everything is true to period,” Fitts explains.

“The exterior of the main house, the colors she chose, the roof tiles, the architecture, and the landscaping. Everything there was intentional.”.

The Victorian home has some Georgian features and has five bedrooms and three full bathrooms.

Industry observers note that “It looks like it could be in The Gilded Age or something like that. There are a total of eight fireplaces in the house. There's parlors, there's dens and small living rooms, and little nooks and crannies throughout the house,” he claims, adding the kitchen is updated appliance-wise, but still has character.

“[There are] stained glass windows throughout, and pressed tin ceilings throughout. It’s insanely intricate.”.

But it’s another room that caught Fitts’ eye.

“They have an old solarium on the lower level that they turned into the coolest bathroom that I've ever seen,” he states.

“You have to be in there to really see it. If you’re entertaining in the house, anyone what visits or goes to that bathroom is just totally wowed. It just it feels like you're in a solarium, but it is a bathroom.”.

According to recent reports, this home has been the seller’s primary residence, with a three-bedroom and three-bathroom cottage for guests and others, especially during events. The seller has operated a small wedding business on the property.

It has been revealed that “She's done it herself. It has been more of a passion for her. It's a wedding venue for small groups and the guest cottage is used as a bridal suite.”.

The groom’s suite and game area are above the barn, and the 4,500-square foot former grist mill is the event space.

Fitts notes most of the wedding ceremonies happen along the waterfront along Pine Log Creek, which creates a stunning backdrop.

It has been revealed that “You pull up to a gate and [after] the gate opens, you go down this long winding driveway with rows of trees and the river that winds through the entire property to your right,” he explains. “Then you turn in up the bluff a little bit, and then it kind of opens up to what you would see in the olden days, like its own little village town.”.

Sources indicate that an old general store and smokehouse are also on the property. Fitts indicates the sellers saw a for sale listing in the newspaper at least 15 years ago, drove up to see it, fell in love with it, and then restored it.

“I was impressed with the story behind it [and] the amount of love that went into owning the property,” he claims, adding there are two kinds of buyers who would be perfect for this estate.

It has been revealed that “It could be a visionary entrepreneur that really wants to lean into making this a hospitality-based venue, spa, bed and breakfast, a true sanctuary. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A secluded retreat tucked beneath one of California’s most photographed landmarks in Big Sur has come on the market for $3.65 million.

The home at 39320 Coast Road sits in Bixby Canyon and is one of only seven residences behind a private gate.

“Millions recognize Bixby Bridge, yet very few will ever experience the landscape beneath it,” says listing agent Michael Hornig of the Strock Team at eXp Realty.

In a recent development, the canyon also comes with a literary history: In 1960, Jack Kerouac retreated to a cabin here owned by Lawrence Ferlinghetti, the poet and co-founder of City Lights Bookstore. His time in the canyon formed the basis for his 1962 novel, “Substantial Sur.” While this is not the original Kerouac cabin, it shares the same setting.

According to Hornig, the canyon has also been home to the film director Sam Peckinpah and the Disney illustrator Ron Dias.

It has been revealed that “There’s an extraordinary feeling about this canyon,” Hornig indicates. “You’re surrounded by a landscape that inspired some of America’s most influential writers, and remarkably, much of that atmosphere of solitude and wilderness remains intact today.”.

Built in 1984, the single-level home has three bedrooms, two full bathrooms, and 1,489 square feet of living space. Vaulted, open-beam ceilings, hardwood floors, and three wood-burning stoves characterize the interiors, as do large windows that frame the surrounding redwoods. A wraparound porch overlooks the forest.

According to recent reports, “Luxury doesn’t always have to be expressed through scale or elaborate architecture,” Hornig claims. “Here, the luxury is the relationship between the home and its surroundings.”.

In a recent development, the property covers two parcels: a 0.79-acre residential lot and an adjacent 0.33-acre creekside lot. It is move-in ready, with a private well, septic system, and electricity. There is also a fenced backyard, storage shed, pasture space and parking for 10 vehicles, including EV charging.

In a recent development, owners share access to a privately held canyon enclave of more than 140 acres. There, a creekside trail winds through redwoods and ferns to a secluded beach beneath the bridge.

“You can walk from your front door through a redwood forest, follow the creek toward the Pacific, and emerge beneath one of the most recognizable bridges in the world,” Hornig says.

Recent findings suggest that next to the property, Brazil Ranch adds about 1,200 acres of U.S. Forest Service land for hiking, hunting, and recreation. The historic Old Coast Road offers miles of biking, horseback riding, and backcountry exploration. Highway 1 is about five minutes away. Carmel, Monterey, and Major Sur’s restaurants and state parks are about 20 minutes away.

“To me, the greatest luxury here is the privilege of belonging to a landscape that most people will only ever admire from a distance,” Hornig indicates. "It's this contrast between one of California’s most recognizable landmarks and the hidden residential community beneath it.".

Sources indicate that on Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to recent reports, according to the entry, the manufacturer claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator remarked.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure users with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

In a recent development, on the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he stated.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

A 25-foot-wide townhouse with a carriage house has just hit the market for $11.95 million in Manhattan’s Carnegie Hill.

Built in 1899, the five-bedroom residence underwent a “no-expense-spared” reconstruction and features 13 newly renovated rooms, each with individually zoned heating and cooling.

Recent findings suggest that “It is certainly very rare for a listing like this townhouse with a carriage house to come on the market in uptown Manhattan,” noted listing agent Daniella G. Schlisser of Brown Harris Stevens. “I don’t recall ever seeing something like this here.”.

The 7,700-square-foot interior was entirely gutted and rebuilt with latest structural steel, plumbing, electrical, and commercial-grade mechanical systems.

Sources indicate that “It has incredible sun and light, which is incredibly unusual for a townhouse,” Schlisser said. “The home is flooded with direct sunlight facing the back and it also gets sun to the north in the front.”.

The six-story dwelling features a garden level that leads to a limestone gallery with custom paneling. There is a separately accessed commercial space offering “continued retail or office use” that could also be transformed into additional living space. French doors open to a bluestone-decked garden with a built-in grill.

“There is a phenomenal amount of space and light, and being a 25-foot-wide townhouse is also rare,” she noted.

Sources indicate that A parlor level boasts a living room with a fireplace and herringbone floors. The nearby formal dining room was designed for grand-scale entertaining. Also on this level is a garden-facing eat-in kitchen with a breakfast bar, granite countertops, custom cabinetry, and high-end appliances.

The third floor has two en-suite bedrooms and a den with coffered ceilings, a wood-burning fireplace, and access to a private terrace overlooking the carriage house.

Two king-sized bedroom suites with custom "study" areas are on the fourth floor.

A lavish primary suite spans the entire fifth floor. It features a south-facing sitting room that opens to a private terrace, a windowed dressing room, and a spa-inspired bathroom with a skylight, soaking tub, and a double vanity.

The sixth floor boasts a “skylit” fitness and wellness room along with a roof terrace “awaiting the next owner’s finishing touch.”.

Schlisser remarked every prospective buyer she has shown the home to is interested in living there full-time.

“Carnegie Hill is a wonderful neighborhood,” she said. “Culturally and educationally, everything is there and the most frequented museums are there as well as some of the best private schools in Manhattan.”.

The detached carriage house has cathedral ceilings, vertical-grain Douglas fir paneling, and a sleeping loft that could be used for guest accommodations or additional recreation space.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the next buyer will be someone who is looking for space and proximity to schools,” Schlisser added. “The style is all fresh but very much a pre-war style. Everything has been done with incredible care. It’s really beautiful.”.

According to recent reports, bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes. Gold isn’t doing much better; oil and stocks have joined the sell-off. The markets are already nervous about the Federal Reserve’s next decision, and yesterday’s FOMC minutes gave us another reason to worry: policymakers are still talking about raising interest rates.

Almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate under their baseline outlook. Two even floated the possibility of a bigger increase if inflation refuses to cool.

This is a nasty combination for markets. Bitcoin fell around 3.2% over 24 hours, gold futures dropped more than 3%, and WTI crude lost around 3%. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Wall Street was mixed, though, with the Nasdaq finishing higher while the Dow and S&P 500 slipped.

Industry observers note that here’s the comparison. In March 2020, the Fed was slashing rates, buying bonds and throwing emergency liquidity at a financial system under immense pressure. Congress approved a $2.2 trillion rescue package to keep households and businesses afloat.

Today, we are watching markets fall while the Fed is possibly making money more expensive.

It has been revealed that october’s FOMC minutes weren’t exactly what markets wanted to hear. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% during its October meeting, but almost all participants believed further increases would likely be appropriate. Two officials also said a hike larger than the usual 25 basis points could be considered if inflation data came in hotter than expected.

And there was more in those minutes than just interest rates. Officials raised concerns about hedge fund leverage and the growing debt tied to artificial intelligence investments. Some financing arrangements could become a problem if investors start questioning enormous AI spending, and whether it will generate the returns companies expect.

The risk is forced selling. Leveraged funds facing losses or investor withdrawals may have to dump assets quickly, potentially pushing prices down further.

According to recent reports, gold has its own problem. A stronger dollar and higher interest rates make it less attractive to investors who can earn a return elsewhere. Bitcoin price, meanwhile, remains vulnerable when traders cut exposure to speculative assets.

The Fed hasn’t declared a financial emergency. Its minutes actually describe the banking system as resilient. But officials are clearly paying attention to risks that could amplify a market shock.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

In a recent development, march 2020 was brutal. COVID-19 lockdowns brought businesses to a standstill. Investors rushed for cash, stocks collapsed, and Bitcoin briefly slipped below $4,000 after sitting near $10,000 just weeks earlier.

The Federal Reserve didn’t wait around. It cut rates by 50 basis points on March 3, then delivered another 100-basis-point cut on March 15. The federal funds target range dropped to 0%–0.25%.

Sources indicate that on March 23, the Fed confirmed unlimited purchases of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities, promising to buy whatever amounts were necessary to support market functioning. It also introduced emergency lending programmes to keep credit flowing.

According to recent reports, president Donald Trump signed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act on March 27. The package included direct payments to eligible Americans, expanded unemployment benefits, and assistance for businesses struggling to survive lockdowns. The Paycheck Protection Program gave small businesses access to loans designed to help them keep employees on payroll.

Sources indicate that the response was enormous, but the economy was facing an extraordinary shutdown. Millions of Americans had lost their jobs, businesses were closing, and normal economic activity had practically disappeared.

Markets eventually bounced back. The S&P 500 recovered its pre-pandemic record by August 2020. Bitcoin climbed above $12,000 during the same month.

In a recent development, the current US economy isn’t in the same position as it was during the pandemic. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, and policymakers are discussing rate increases rather than cuts.

Recent findings suggest that slashing rates to zero and flooding markets with liquidity might help asset prices. It could also make inflation worse. Another multitrillion-dollar spending package would face an entirely different argument in Congress, especially without a pandemic-style economic shutdown.

The Fed doesn’t have to choose between doing nothing and repeating the 2020 rescue. If banks struggle to fund themselves or credit markets start freezing, it can step in with emergency lending and liquidity operations. That’s a much narrower response than another round of unlimited bond purchases.

The Fed’s concerns about leveraged hedge funds and AI financing could become more relevant if investors start selling indiscriminately. A market correction is one thing. Forced selling spreading through the financial system is another.

In a recent development, at the moment, there’s no evidence that we’re facing another March 2020. The banking system remains resilient, and falling Bitcoin prices alone won’t trigger a government bailout.

Recent findings suggest that but the Fed has a problem that didn’t exist in quite the same way during the pandemic. It may need to protect financial stability without giving up its fight against inflation. In 2020, Washington opened the taps. This time, we wait and see, and Bitcoin price will survive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engel & Völkers announced an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.

Brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into fresh markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it plans to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

Industry observers note that eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. IRES MLS welcomed back a former staffer to run operations, and Howard Hanna Portside added an agent in Massachusetts.

Industry observers note that engel & Völkers expanded into Aruba with license partners Zobaida Akkari and Richard Franken, Aruba-based entrepreneurs with backgrounds in real estate, luxury sales, hospitality and tourism. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the organization.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, stated in a statement.

Industry observers note that realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the company. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, says it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa noted in a statement.

Industry observers note that rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the organization.

In a recent development, jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

Baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen mentioned in a statement.

Dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

Sources indicate that “Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs said in a statement.

Sources indicate that IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl said in a statement.

Howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the tech giant.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter remarked in a statement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The home where Woodrow Wilson lived as a professor before becoming president has hit the market in Princeton, NJ for $5.85 million.
  • The Tudor Revival at 82 Library Place was built in 1896 for Wilson and he lived there with his wife, Ellen, and their three children until 1902, when he became president of Princeton University and moved on campus.
  • The home was first listed in May 2025 for $6.5 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The home where Woodrow Wilson lived as a professor before becoming president has hit the market in Princeton, NJ for $5.85 million.

The Tudor Revival at 82 Library Place was built in 1896 for Wilson and he lived there with his wife, Ellen, and their three children until 1902, when he became president of Princeton University and moved on campus.

The home was first listed in May 2025 for $6.5 million.

“Wilson and his wife had a lot of input in the design and finishes chosen for the home, which included double stained-glass doors from the Sears catalog,” notes listing agent Barbara Blackwell of Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty.

Industry observers note that the estate is one of only two working homes in the U.S. designed and built by a president, the other being Monticello, according to the listing.

Blackwell indicates the house has had 19 owners since the Wilsons, including Princeton University itself, which used the home as faculty housing during the Great Depression.

Recent findings suggest that the current owners spent seven years restoring the property with architect Ron Berlin and Baxter Construction. The award-winning project brought back the original beams and woodwork and re-glassed the leaded windows. It also gave the home a distinct sense of presidential charm, making it easy to imagine Wilson tucked among its interiors.

The work also restored the stucco and timber exterior, added a cedar shake roof and a generator, and updated all mechanical systems.

In a recent development, the three-story home includes seven bedrooms and 5.5 bathrooms. Wilson once taught students in the spacious foyer, which opens to a wood-paneled library the current owners added. Stained-glass pocket doors lead to a dining room with a commissioned mural of campus landmarks.

Sources indicate that the kitchen pairs restored original cabinetry with new matching pieces. It also has a copper drainboard sink, a working dumbwaiter, and a double Wolf range. Nearby, a new glass-roofed sunroom with a wet bar overlooks the grounds.

“The sunroom is a perfect blends interior and exterior with views of the gardens and flowering trees,” Blackwell says.

According to recent reports, of the four bedrooms on the second floor, one is a soundproofed primary suite with a coffee bar and a radiant-heated marble bathroom that opens onto a balcony. The skylit third floor contains three more bedrooms, a bathroom, laundry and a cedar walk-in closet.

In a recent development, outside, the recently redesigned gardens surround two patios, a fountain and a koi pond. The 0.74-acre lot also has a circular driveway lined with boxwoods, an office in a former porte cochere and a restored, oversized two-car garage in the same Tudor style as the house.

The property is in Princeton’s Western Section and backs up to the current home of the university’s president. Nassau Street’s shops and restaurants are a short walk away.

It has been revealed that “This home represents a substantial piece of history with all the modern conveniences of a upcoming home,” Blackwell says. The owner’s collection of Wilson books and memorabilia can be bought separately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

It’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

It has been revealed that to leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

Season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

At the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio remarked the injury took two or three months to heal.

Industry observers note that the following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He remarked he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

What follows is the conversation, edited for length and clarity.

According to recent reports, I think for me, 100 percent, the heat. I think I anticipated intense heat and intense humidity, but you don’t know what it’s like until you really feel it … It was so unbearably hot, and in our barracks that we slept in, there was no windows, and when you were inside, you actually couldn’t tell like what was even happening out there. But it was almost like … “Good, let me be locked in this metal box because the outside is crazy.”.

Mauricio: I think for me, it was just the intensity of what a jungle really is. The first day we got there … when we were all showering and waiting to shower, there was a scorpion crawling on my leg, about to go in my boot, which I felt it and took it off just in the nick of time. Because if it went in my boot, it would have stung me, no question, right?

Recent findings suggest that alexia: It’s so hard to choose because literally every single thing was hard. Part of me wanted to say the car rides leading up to each challenge, because we didn’t know what was coming, and it was always so intense in the car. My heart would start pounding … the bottom line is the hardest part is just making sure that your mindset is correct [in] doing all these things and waking up each day and moving forward because that’s really what gets going is just moving forward and choosing to keep on going.

It has been revealed that mauricio: Yeah, I think Alexia nailed it. I mean, for me, it was really all about the little victories. The only way to survive is by looking at small victories, small steps … we used to say just make it to the next meal, just make it to the next day, just make it to tonight.

According to recent reports, for me, the hardest part was leaving, was having to voluntarily withdraw. I did not want to have a medical withdrawal, so I didn’t want to go see the doctor and have them withdraw me.

Mauricio: Not one thing for me. What about you, Alexia?

Alexia: No. There’s nothing about this that’s easy.

Alexia: We loved everybody so much. I mean, we still talk all the time, and we still love each other so much. The words of affirmation we all told each other to this day are so special … But I think my first answer would have to be Candace [Cameron] Bure … she’s so strong, and we got looped together for a bunch of things because of our height similarities.

Mauricio: Well, I have to say that the person who surprised me the most was Alexia … the strength of her mind, her strength and what she did was extraordinary.

Sources indicate that alexia: Oh my god, yeah. Are you kidding me? All the time.

Alexia: Definitely thought it was pretty cool. It was an honor to be punched in the chest by DJ Tanner … I actually appreciated very much that she didn’t hold back because I just felt like I was treated like an equal, an individual.

In a recent development, alexia: I’ve never punched anyone or anything … the second she threw the first punch, I knew she was so much stronger than me. But my goal was to just not fall down. I really didn’t want to fall down, so I was just trying to stay up the entire time. It felt like a fight went on for so long.

It has been revealed that and I remember thinking, like, “Are we gonna go there? … That would be so inappropriate. Everything’s in my power, and I’m not gonna go there” … Once I was finally in there, I understood why they asked … you’re stripped down to the very core of you, and you’re tired, and you’re pushing yourself, and you’re emotional, you’re exhausted … And Bre Tiesi, she got emotional, and [she noted to me] ”I haven’t cried in years. I hate crying.”.

It was really about discovering and repurposing the strength that I always felt that I had, but there was a time that I had felt that I had lost that.

And each night, as I was going to sleep, I just remember thinking to myself, “This is so rewarding, and this is so empowering, and this is so incredible for someone that has gone through what I have” … some people [feel like they] get their voice back. I always felt like I had my voice, but I feel like I got to discover a strength I always knew I had that someone had pushed me to question, and feeling that was just incredibly healing.

Alexia: No, not my parents. I had told two of my sisters before, and then, obviously, I told my dad on the course, and then, before the show aired, I ended up calling my mom and [sister] Portia to tell them because I obviously did not want that to be the first time they read it. And even though I spoke about it on the course, I’m still very, very afraid to tell them afterward, too.

Sources indicate that mauricio: It was extremely difficult … I was just proud of Alexia every single day, every single moment … hearing that story was just another revelation of her conquering and finally talking about something that I wish she never held back … I just wanted to reach out and just hug her. But by the same token, I also wanted to give her space and let her be her in that moment that she was sharing with everybody. So there was like a lot of stuff going through my mind.

There was anger toward this kid that did this … But [watching her let go of it] was beautiful to watch … from my perspective, it was like, “Do I reach over and become a dad and just give her a big hug, or do I let her go through this moment, psychologically speaking, of letting it all come out?”.

And I was just proud of her all the way around.

It has been revealed that in hindsight, I love that she was able to share that, get it off her chest with us, with everybody, with the world. I think it’s super powerful.

Yes, I live by a lot of different small philosophies. Certainty versus doubt. Momentum is the cure of all fears. All of these are the different things where you just have to move forward, right? In order to accomplish something, you kind of just have to move forward, right? … the moment that I went from being an agent to opening up a brokerage, you jump off the cliff; you hope the parachute catches.

According to recent reports, to today … here we are in a really difficult real estate market. I mean, it is not fun out there right now whatsoever. Yet [The Agency is] still growing. We’re still putting money out there. We’re still doing things right. So yeah, to me that’s just a philosophy that I always live by.

According to recent reports, mauricio: I don’t know. We’ll just keep going. I really like that show Traitors. I would love to be on that show. That could be a fun one for me, so I’m putting that out into the universe.

Alexia: My dream would be to do a reality TV show with my family … We did Buying Beverly Hills, and we’ve done Real Housewives for like [16] years now. But we’ve never done something all of us together, just us, and I think that’ll be really cool.

In a recent development, mauricio: I’m going to leave that one on the table. If anything, it’s for 2030. There’s still plenty of time to do that and make that decision. But I love LA, and I think I can help LA a lot. I think we live in an amazing city, and if the moment comes, and I’m set up in the right position in the business and I feel like I can actually win, I might do it. But I wouldn’t do it if I didn’t feel like I could actually win.

Mauricio: It’s an absolute mess, what’s going on in our in our in our industry right now, particularly with the listings. My take is, it’s quite simple. I think that there’s a lot of change that’s happening. I believe that it’s somewhere in the middle. Like I do everything.

In a recent development, I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. I feel like there’s a lot happening right now in the industry where everybody’s really looking out for themselves: the MLSs, NAR, Compass.

Actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a substantial, big fight. But in the meantime, this Clear Cooperation Policy is what is allowing them to keep all the listings to themselves and not share them … The PLS is exactly what that was, and I still think that if Clear Cooperation Policy didn’t pass, it would have been an amazing business to have right now.

In a recent development, mauricio: We are really positioned as the premier luxury brokerage firm outside of Compass right now. They’ve got Sotheby’s, they’ve got Christie’s, they’ve got all of those different brands, and we’re the only independent luxury brokerage firm out there right now.

So I’m excited to be in that position. Competitors make you better every single day … I’m excited in terms of where we sit, where we stand in a very difficult time; I’m not excited about the market. We really need to do some things to improve it. We’ve had three years of very, very difficult conditions, and it’s going to be very difficult for people to survive. And those that do survive will come out better.

I think we’re in a good position to survive, but we’ve got our work cut out for us over the next year, year and a half. But we’ll continue to grow. We’ll continue to expand, and I’m excited to just be a part of this industry. But man, it’s hard out there right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The coming week brings a number of key indicators and fresh research from the Realtor.com Economics team, despite the holiday schedule for Thanksgiving Day.

On Monday, upcoming research from senior economist Hannah Jones reveals that many Americans won't be traveling far to visit their parents for the holiday. That’s because a third of American adults under 35 years old still live in their parents’ home.

On Wednesday, senior economist Jiayi Xu has our third-quarter International Demand report, showing where home shoppers from different countries are looking at U.S. homes.

Also on Wednesday, coming out early due to the Thanksgiving holiday, senior economist Jake Krimmel will analyze our weekly housing data for clues on the latest housing market trends in real time.

For economic indicators being released next week, we’ll see the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Index on Tuesday, along with new-home sales and the Freddie Mac mortgage rate on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that the Case-Shiller Index is expected to show national home price growth holding near 2% through September, after the national index rose 2.1% year over year through August. Annual gains have climbed since the spring, but slower median sales price growth and softer contract activity this summer suggest the pickup may be running out of steam.

According to recent reports, upcoming-home sales are likely to show another weak month in October, after falling 5.3% year over year in September. The existing-home segment saw softer pending home sales and home purchase closings last month as buyers are faced with affordability challenges due to high mortgage rates.

Despite more builders offering mortgage rate buydowns, the newly introduced-home segment is expected to be slowed down as well, as buyers’ budgets are stretched thin.

One thing I’ll be watching closely is the median newly introduced-home sales price, which has been lower than the median existing-home sales price for much of 2026, an intriguing result that mostly stems from where the new homes being sold are located.

The Freddie Mac average mortgage rate, which will come out on Wednesday instead of its usual Thursday, is likely to remain in the low-7% range, as the 10-Year Treasury yield remains elevated above 5% in advance of the expected rate hike by the Federal Reserve.

For full reports, the Market Clock, and raw housing data, visit realtor.com/research.

His career has focused on the intersection of technology and real estate, and Joel has appeared live on CNN, Yahoo Finance, and Fox 7 Austin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Industry observers note that binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its customers and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that consumers will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Users are strongly advised to enhancement and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

It has been revealed that in related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.
